use PHPStan\Analyser\Scope;
use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;
use PHPStan\Rules\Rule;
use PHPStan\Rules\RuleErrorBuilder;

use function sprintf;

/**
 * Requires exceptions thrown inside a catch block to chain the caught one.
 *
 * Wrapping a low-level exception in a domain exception is good practice, but
 * only when the original exception travels along as $previous. Otherwise the
 * root cause and its stack trace are unrecoverable at the top-level handler.
 *
 * @implements Rule<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Catch_>
 */
final class RequireExceptionChainingRule implements Rule
{
    /** @readonly */
    private CatchThrowCollector $catchThrowCollector;

    /** @readonly */
    private ThrowChainEvaluator $throwChainEvaluator;

    /**
     * Creates the rule from throw collection and chain evaluation.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?CatchThrowCollector $catchThrowCollector = null,
        ?ThrowChainEvaluator $throwChainEvaluator = null,
    ) {
        $this->catchThrowCollector = $catchThrowCollector ?? new CatchThrowCollector();
        $this->throwChainEvaluator = $throwChainEvaluator ?? new ThrowChainEvaluator();
    }

    /**
     * @return class-string<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Catch_>
     */
    public function getNodeType(): string
    {
        return \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Catch_::class;
    }

    /**
     * @param \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Catch_ $node
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function processNode(\PhpParser\Node $node, Scope $scope): array
    {
        unset($scope);

        $variable = $node->var;
        $caughtVariableName = $variable instanceof Variable && is_string($variable->name) ? $variable->name : null;

        $errors = [];
        foreach ($this->catchThrowCollector->collect($node->stmts) as $throw) {
            if (!$this->throwChainEvaluator->violates($throw, $caughtVariableName)) {
                continue;
            }

            if ($caughtVariableName === null) {
                $caughtTypes = implode('|', array_map(static fn (Name $name): string => $name->toString(), $node->types));
                $message = sprintf(
                    'Bind the caught %s to a variable and pass it to the exception thrown in this catch block, e.g. as the $previous constructor argument. Throwing a new exception without chaining discards the original failure and its stack trace.',
                    $caughtTypes
                );
            } else {
                $message = sprintf(
                    'Pass the caught $%s to the exception thrown in this catch block, e.g. as the $previous constructor argument. Throwing a new exception without chaining discards the original failure and its stack trace.',
                    $caughtVariableName
                );
            }

            $errors[] = RuleErrorBuilder::message($message)
                ->identifier('customRules.unchainedRethrow')
                ->line($throw->getStartLine())
                ->build();
        }

        return $errors;
    }
}

/**
 * Requires list<V> when a property or callable visibly owns a list literal.
 *
 * @implements Rule<Stmt>
 */
final class RequireListForArrayLiteralRule implements Rule
{
    /** @readonly */
    private ListTypeDeclarationInspector $declarations;

    /** @readonly */
    private FixedListExpressionInspector $expressions;

    /**
     * Creates the rule from PHPDoc and literal expression inspection.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?ListTypeDeclarationInspector $declarations = null,
        ?FixedListExpressionInspector $expressions = null,
    ) {
        $this->declarations = $declarations ?? new ListTypeDeclarationInspector();
        $this->expressions = $expressions ?? new FixedListExpressionInspector();
    }

    /**
     * @return class-string<Stmt>
     */
    public function getNodeType(): string
    {
        return Stmt::class;
    }

    /**
     * @param Stmt $node
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function processNode(\PhpParser\Node $node, Scope $scope): array
    {
        if ($node instanceof Property) {
            return $this->propertyErrors($node);
        }
        if ($node instanceof ClassMethod || $node instanceof Function_) {
            return $this->returnErrors($node);
        }

        return [];
    }

    /**
     * Builds errors for list-valued property initializers.
     *
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function propertyErrors(Property $property): array
    {
        $docComment = $property->getDocComment();
        if ($docComment === null || stripos($docComment->getText(), 'array') === false) {
            return [];
        }

        $declarations = $this->declarations->propertyDeclarations($docComment->getText());
        $errors = [];
        foreach ($property->props as $item) {
            if (!$item->default instanceof Array_ || !$this->expressions->isNonEmptyList($item->default)) {
                continue;
            }
            $propertyName = '$' . $item->name->toString();
            foreach ($declarations as $declaration) {
                if ($declaration['variable'] !== '' && $declaration['variable'] !== $propertyName) {
                    continue;
                }
                $errors[] = RuleErrorBuilder::message(sprintf(
                    'Replace "%s" with "%s" in %s on %s; %s is initialized with a non-empty list literal, so declare its zero-based contiguous keys as part of the property type.',
                    $declaration['type'],
                    $declaration['replacement'],
                    $declaration['tag'],
                    $propertyName,
                    $propertyName
                ))
                    ->identifier('customRules.arrayLiteralListType')
                    ->line($property->getStartLine())
                    ->build();
            }
        }

        return $errors;
    }

    /**
     * Builds errors for list-valued callable returns.
     *
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function returnErrors(ClassMethod|Function_ $callable): array
    {
        $docComment = $callable->getDocComment();
        if ($docComment === null || stripos($docComment->getText(), 'array') === false) {
            return [];
        }
        if (!$this->expressions->callableReturnsFixedLists($callable)) {
            return [];
        }

        $callableName = sprintf('%s()', $callable->name->toString());
        $errors = [];
        foreach ($this->declarations->returnDeclarations($docComment->getText()) as $declaration) {
            $errors[] = RuleErrorBuilder::message(sprintf(
                'Replace "%s" with "%s" in %s on %s; %s returns a non-empty list literal, so declare its zero-based contiguous keys as part of the return type.',
                $declaration['type'],
                $declaration['replacement'],
                $declaration['tag'],
                $callableName,
                $callableName
            ))
                ->identifier('customRules.arrayLiteralListType')
                ->line($callable->getStartLine())
                ->build();
        }

        return $errors;
    }
}

use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\Path\RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher;

/**
 * Collects descriptive PHPDoc errors in restricted test classes.
 */
final class DescriptivePhpDocErrorCollector
{
    /** @readonly */
    private DescriptivePhpDocTextDetector $textDetector;

    /**
     * Creates a collector from namespace matching and PHPDoc text detection.
     */
    public function __construct(
        /** @readonly */
        private RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher $namespaceMatcher,
        ?DescriptivePhpDocTextDetector $textDetector = null,
    ) {
        $this->textDetector = $textDetector ?? new DescriptivePhpDocTextDetector();
    }

    /**
     * Returns descriptive PHPDoc errors for the class-like node.
     *
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function errors(\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike $node): array
    {
        if (!$this->namespaceMatcher->matches($node)) {
            return [];
        }

        $className = $node->name !== null ? $node->name->toString() : '(anonymous)';
        $errors = [];

        $docComment = $node->getDocComment();
        if ($docComment !== null && $this->textDetector->has($docComment->getText())) {
            $errors[] = RuleErrorBuilder::message(
                sprintf(
                    'Remove descriptive text from PHPDoc on test class %s. Keep only annotations such as @extends.',
                    $className
                )
            )
                ->identifier('customRules.testClassDescriptivePhpDoc')
                ->line($node->getStartLine())
                ->build();
        }

        foreach ($node->getMethods() as $method) {
            $methodDoc = $method->getDocComment();
            if ($methodDoc === null || !$this->textDetector->has($methodDoc->getText())) {
                continue;
            }

            $errors[] = RuleErrorBuilder::message(
                sprintf(
                    'Remove descriptive text from PHPDoc on method %s::%s(). Keep only annotations such as @dataProvider.',
                    $className,
                    $method->name->toString()
                )
            )
                ->identifier('customRules.testClassDescriptivePhpDoc')
                ->line($method->getStartLine())
                ->build();
        }

        return $errors;
    }
}

{
    /** @readonly */
    private OverrideAttributeDetector $overrideAttributeDetector;

    public function __construct(?OverrideAttributeDetector $overrideAttributeDetector = null)

    public function allows(

namespace Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\ClassDesign;

use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;

/**
 * Inspects method and static calls for direct magic method calls.
 */
final class MagicMethodCallInspector
{
    /** @readonly */
    private MagicMethodRegistry $magicMethodRegistry;

    /** @readonly */
    private MagicMethodCallErrorBuilder $errorBuilder;

    /**
     * Creates an inspector from magic method registry and error building.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?MagicMethodRegistry $magicMethodRegistry = null,
        ?MagicMethodCallErrorBuilder $errorBuilder = null,
    ) {
        $this->magicMethodRegistry = $magicMethodRegistry ?? new MagicMethodRegistry();
        $this->errorBuilder = $errorBuilder ?? new MagicMethodCallErrorBuilder();
    }

    /**
     * Returns direct magic method call errors for the expression.
     *
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function errors(\PhpParser\Node\Expr $node): array
    {
        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Expr\MethodCall) {
            if (!$node->name instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Identifier) {
                return [];
            }

            $methodName = $node->name->toString();
            return $this->magicMethodRegistry->isMagic($methodName) ? [$this->errorBuilder->error($methodName, $node->getStartLine())] : [];
        }

        if (!$node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Expr\StaticCall) {
            return [];
        }

        if (!$node->name instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Identifier) {
            return [];
        }

        $methodName = $node->name->toString();
        if (!$this->magicMethodRegistry->isMagic($methodName)) {
            return [];
        }

        if ($node->class instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Name && strtolower($node->class->toString()) === 'parent') {
            return [];
        }

        return [$this->errorBuilder->error($methodName, $node->getStartLine())];
    }
}

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\ExceptionHandling;

use function array_pop;

use PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Finally_;

use PhpParser\NodeTraverser;
use PhpParser\NodeVisitorAbstract;
use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\ThrownExpression;

/**
 * Collects throw statements that escape the traversed statement list.
 *
 * Tracks enclosing try/catch nesting so that a throw inside a try block
 * records the catch types guarding it, while throws inside catch and finally
 * blocks are not protected by their own try. Nested closures, arrow
 * functions, and anonymous classes are skipped because their throws do not
 * escape the enclosing method at declaration time.
 */
final class ThrowSiteVisitor extends NodeVisitorAbstract
{
    /** @var list<array{types: list<Name>, active: bool}> */
    private array $tryFrames = [];

    /** @var list<array{var: ?string, types: list<Name>}> */
    private array $catchBindings = [];

    /** @var list<ThrowSite> */
    private array $sites = [];

    /** @readonly */
    private ThrownExpression $thrown;

    /**
     * Creates the visitor from what reads the thrown expression.
     */
    public function __construct(?ThrownExpression $thrown = null)
    {
        $this->thrown = $thrown ?? new ThrownExpression();
    }

    /**
     * Tracks try/catch nesting and records throw statements.
     *
     * @return ?int a traversal instruction, or null to continue
     */
    #[Override]
    public function enterNode(Node $node): ?int
    {
        if ($node instanceof Closure || $node instanceof ArrowFunction || $node instanceof Class_) {
            return NodeTraverser::DONT_TRAVERSE_CHILDREN;
        }

        if ($node instanceof TryCatch) {
            $types = [];
            foreach ($node->catches as $catch) {
                foreach ($catch->types as $type) {
                    $types[] = $type;
                }
            }
            $this->tryFrames[] = ['types' => $types, 'active' => true];

            return null;
        }

        if ($node instanceof Catch_ || $node instanceof Finally_) {
            $frameIndex = count($this->tryFrames) - 1;
            if ($frameIndex >= 0) {
                $this->tryFrames[$frameIndex]['active'] = false;
            }
            if ($node instanceof Catch_) {
                $variable = $node->var;
                $variableName = $variable instanceof Variable && is_string($variable->name) ? $variable->name : null;
                $this->catchBindings[] = ['var' => $variableName, 'types' => array_values($node->types)];
            }

            return null;
        }

        if ($this->thrown->isThrow($node)) {
            $this->recordThrow($node);
        }

        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Restores try/catch tracking when leaving try, catch, and finally nodes.
     *
     * @return null always null to keep the node unchanged
     */
    #[Override]
    public function leaveNode(Node $node): ?int
    {
        if ($node instanceof TryCatch) {
            array_pop($this->tryFrames);

            return null;
        }

        if ($node instanceof Catch_ || $node instanceof Finally_) {
            $frameIndex = count($this->tryFrames) - 1;
            if ($frameIndex >= 0) {
                $this->tryFrames[$frameIndex]['active'] = true;
            }
            if ($node instanceof Catch_) {
                array_pop($this->catchBindings);
            }
        }

        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Records one throw statement with its thrown names and active guards.
     */
    public function recordThrow(Node $node): void
    {
        $thrownNames = [];
        $expr = $this->thrown->of($node);
        if ($expr instanceof New_ && $expr->class instanceof Name) {
            $thrownNames = [$expr->class];
        } elseif ($expr instanceof Variable && is_string($expr->name)) {
            for ($index = count($this->catchBindings) - 1; $index >= 0; $index--) {
                if ($this->catchBindings[$index]['var'] === $expr->name) {
                    $thrownNames = $this->catchBindings[$index]['types'];
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        if ($thrownNames === []) {
            return;
        }

        $guardNames = [];
        foreach ($this->tryFrames as $frame) {
            if (!$frame['active']) {
                continue;
            }
            foreach ($frame['types'] as $type) {
                $guardNames[] = $type;
            }
        }

        $this->sites[] = new ThrowSite($thrownNames, $guardNames, $node->getStartLine());
    }

    /**
     * Returns the throw sites collected during traversal.
     *
     * @return list<ThrowSite>
     */
    public function sites(): array
    {
        return $this->sites;
    }
}

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\ExceptionHandling;

use PhpParser\NodeTraverser;

/**
 * Collects the throw statements directly inside one catch block body.
 */
final class CatchThrowCollector
{
    /**
     * Returns the throw statements that belong to the given catch body.
     *
     * @param array<\PhpParser\Node\Stmt> $stmts
     * @return list<\PhpParser\Node>
     */
    public function collect(array $stmts): array
    {
        $traverser = new NodeTraverser();
        $visitor = new CatchThrowVisitor();
        $traverser->addVisitor($visitor);
        $traverser->traverse($stmts);

        return $visitor->throws();
    }
}

use function is_string;

use PhpParser\Node;
use PhpParser\Node\Expr\CallLike;
use PhpParser\Node\Expr\Variable;
use PhpParser\NodeFinder;
use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\ThrownExpression;

/**
 * Decides whether a throw inside a catch block chains the caught exception.
 */
final class ThrowChainEvaluator
{
    /** @readonly */
    private ThrownExpression $thrown;

    /**
     * Creates the evaluator from what reads the thrown expression.
     */
    public function __construct(?ThrownExpression $thrown = null)
    {
        $this->thrown = $thrown ?? new ThrownExpression();
    }

    /**
     * Reports whether the throw creates a new exception without referencing the caught one.
     *
     * Only instantiations and calls are evaluated; rethrowing a variable is
     * never a violation because the exception object itself is preserved.
     */
    public function violates(Node $throw, ?string $caughtVariableName): bool
    {
        $expr = $this->thrown->of($throw);
        if (!$expr instanceof CallLike) {
            return false;
        }

        if ($caughtVariableName === null) {
            return true;
        }

        $reference = (new NodeFinder())->findFirst(
            $expr,
            static fn (Node $node): bool => $node instanceof Variable
                && is_string($node->name)
                && $node->name === $caughtVariableName,
        );

        return $reference === null;
    }
}
# NoNonPublicMethodRule

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Identifier | `customRules.nonPublicMethod` |
| Scope | All class-like methods except constructors |
| Configurable | No |

## What It Detects

Reports private methods everywhere, and protected methods except in abstract classes, traits, and override methods. Constructors are never reported, whatever their visibility.

```php
final class InvoiceService
{
    public function issue(Invoice $invoice): Receipt
    {
        $this->validate($invoice);
        return $this->createReceipt($invoice);
    }

    // ERROR: Move private method validate() out of InvoiceService into a focused collaborator.
    private function validate(Invoice $invoice): void
    {
        // ...
    }
}
```

Protected methods are allowed when they are intentionally part of an inheritance boundary:

```php
abstract class ImportTemplate
{
    public function import(File $file): Result
    {
        return $this->parse($file);
    }

    protected function parse(File $file): Result
    {
        // ...
    }
}
```

A private or protected constructor is allowed. Restricting construction is how PHP expresses singletons, named constructors, and other controlled-instantiation designs, so it is an API decision rather than a hidden responsibility:

```php
final class Registry
{
    private static ?self $instance = null;

    private function __construct()
    {
    }

    public static function instance(): self
    {
        return self::$instance ??= new self();
    }
}
```

## Why This Is an Error

Private and non-override protected methods often hide additional responsibilities inside a class. The rule is not a visibility preference and should not be fixed by changing method access modifiers. If a behavior is complex enough to need its own named method, that behavior usually deserves one of these outcomes:

1. **It belongs to the type**: Make it part of the public behavior and test it through that public API.

2. **It is a separate responsibility**: Extract it to a focused collaborator with its own public API.

3. **It is an inheritance extension point**: Keep it protected only on an abstract class, trait, or override method.

## How to Fix

Extract hidden behavior to a focused collaborator:

```php
final class InvoiceService
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly InvoiceValidator $validator,
    ) {
    }

    public function issue(Invoice $invoice): Receipt
    {
        $this->validator->validate($invoice);
        return Receipt::fromInvoice($invoice);
    }
}

final class InvoiceValidator
{
    public function validate(Invoice $invoice): void
    {
        // ...
    }
}
```

        $inspector = new ThrowsDeclarationInspector();

    public function refactor(Node $node): ?Node

        $comments = [];
        $changed = false;
        foreach ($node->getComments() as $comment) {

            if ($replacement !== null) {

        if (!$changed) {

        $node->setAttribute('comments', $comments);

        return $node;

    /**
     * Leaves inline prose mentions and ambiguous PHPDoc lines for manual review.
     */
    public function withoutSuppression(Comment $comment, ForbiddenCommentPattern $pattern): ?Comment
    {
        if (!$pattern->isHandled($comment->getText())) {

use PHPStan\PhpDocParser\Ast\PhpDoc\VarTagValueNode;

use PHPStan\PhpDocParser\Ast\Type\IdentifierTypeNode;
use PHPStan\PhpDocParser\Ast\Type\IntersectionTypeNode;

use PHPStan\PhpDocParser\Ast\Type\UnionTypeNode;

use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\PhpDoc\FixedListExpressionInspector;
use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\PhpDoc\ListTypeDeclarationInspector;
use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\PhpDoc\RulePhpDocParser;

/**
 * Narrows literal-owned array declarations to list contracts for review.
 */
final class RequireListForArrayLiteralRector extends AbstractRector
{
    /**
     * @return list<class-string<Node>>
     */
    #[Override]
    public function getNodeTypes(): array
    {
        return [Property::class, ClassMethod::class, Function_::class];
    }

    /**
     * Changes only owned return or property types, preserving parameter types.
     *
     * @param Property|ClassMethod|Function_ $node
     */
    public function refactor(Node $node): ?Node
    {
        $doc = $node->getDocComment();
        $expressions = new FixedListExpressionInspector();
        if ($doc === null) {
            return null;
        }
        if ($node instanceof Property) {
            if (count($node->props) !== 1 || !$node->props[0]->default instanceof Array_ || !$expressions->isNonEmptyList($node->props[0]->default)) {
                return null;
            }
        } elseif (!$expressions->callableReturnsFixedLists($node)) {
            return null;
        }

        $parsed = (new RulePhpDocParser())->parse($doc->getText());
        $before = (string) $parsed;
        $tagNames = $node instanceof Property ? ['@var', '@phpstan-var', '@psalm-var'] : ['@return', '@phpstan-return', '@psalm-return'];
        foreach ($tagNames as $tagName) {
            foreach ($parsed->getTagsByName($tagName) as $tag) {
                if ($tag->value instanceof VarTagValueNode && $node instanceof Property) {
                    if ($tag->value->variableName !== '' && $tag->value->variableName !== '$' . $node->props[0]->name->toString()) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    $this->narrow($tag->value->type);
                } elseif ($tag->value instanceof ReturnTagValueNode) {
                    $this->narrow($tag->value->type);
                }
            }
        }
        if ((string) $parsed === $before) {
            return null;
        }
        $node->setDocComment(new Doc((string) $parsed));

        return $node;
    }

    /**
     * Rewrites direct union/intersection branches without changing nested value types.
     */
    public function narrow(TypeNode $type): void
    {
        if ($type instanceof GenericTypeNode && (new ListTypeDeclarationInspector())->isArrayIntType($type)) {
            $type->type = new IdentifierTypeNode('list');
            $type->genericTypes = [$type->genericTypes[1]];
            $type->variances = [$type->variances[1] ?? GenericTypeNode::VARIANCE_INVARIANT];
        } elseif ($type instanceof NullableTypeNode) {
            $this->narrow($type->type);
        } elseif ($type instanceof UnionTypeNode || $type instanceof IntersectionTypeNode) {
            foreach ($type->types as $member) {
                $this->narrow($member);
            }
        }
    }
}

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Toolkit\Rector;

use Override;

use Rector\Contract\Rector\ConfigurableRectorInterface;
use Rector\Rector\AbstractRector;
use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\Path\RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher;
use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\TestClass\DescriptivePhpDocTextDetector;

/**
 * Removes leading test PHPDoc prose while retaining complete annotation bodies.
 */
final class ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector extends AbstractRector implements ConfigurableRectorInterface
{
    /**
     * @var list<string>
     */
    private array $prefixes = ['Tests\\Unit', 'Tests\\Integration'];

    /**
     * Sets the same restricted namespace prefixes as the corresponding PHPStan rule.
     *
     * @param list<string> $configuration
     */
    public function configure(array $configuration): void
    {
        $this->prefixes = $configuration;
    }

    /**
     * @return list<class-string<Node>>
     */
    #[Override]
    public function getNodeTypes(): array
    {
        return [ClassLike::class];
    }

    /**
     * Removes prose only from restricted test classes and their methods.
     *
     * @param ClassLike $node
     */
    public function refactor(Node $node): ?Node
    {
        if (!(new RestrictedTestNamespaceMatcher($this->prefixes))->matches($node)) {
            return null;
        }
        $changed = $this->removeProse($node);
        foreach ($node->getMethods() as $method) {
            $changed = $this->removeProse($method) || $changed;
        }

        return $changed ? $node : null;
    }

    /**
     * Keeps tag continuation lines, including multiline shapes and examples.
     */
    public function removeProse(Node $node): bool
    {
        $doc = $node->getDocComment();
        if ($doc === null || !(new DescriptivePhpDocTextDetector())->has($doc->getText())) {
            return false;
        }
        $body = substr($doc->getText(), 3, -2);
        if (preg_match('/(?:^|\R)[\t *]*(@[a-zA-Z][\s\S]*)/', $body, $match) === 1) {
            $node->setDocComment(new Doc("/**\n * " . rtrim($match[1]) . "\n */"));
        } else {
            $node->setAttribute('comments', array_values(array_filter($node->getComments(), static fn ($comment): bool => $comment !== $doc)));
        }

        return true;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\TestAssertion;

use function count;

use PHPStan\Analyser\Scope;
use PHPStan\Rules\IdentifierRuleError;
use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\CallArgumentResolver;
use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\CallMethodNameResolver;
use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\ClassStringExpressionResolver;
use Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared\PhpUnitCallTargetMatcher;

/**
 * Detects PHPUnit assertInstanceOf() calls guaranteed by static types.
 */
final class AssertInstanceOfRedundancyInspector
{
    /** @readonly */
    private CallMethodNameResolver $methodNameResolver;

    /** @readonly */
    private CallArgumentResolver $argumentResolver;

    /** @readonly */
    private ClassStringExpressionResolver $classStringResolver;

    /** @readonly */
    private PhpUnitCallTargetMatcher $targetMatcher;

    /** @readonly */
    private NoRedundantAssertInstanceOfErrorBuilder $errorBuilder;

    /** @readonly */
    private AssertInstanceOfTypeMatcher $typeMatcher;

    /**
     * Creates an inspector from call parsing and error-building collaborators.
     */
    public function __construct(
        ?CallMethodNameResolver $methodNameResolver = null,
        ?CallArgumentResolver $argumentResolver = null,
        ?ClassStringExpressionResolver $classStringResolver = null,
        ?PhpUnitCallTargetMatcher $targetMatcher = null,
        ?NoRedundantAssertInstanceOfErrorBuilder $errorBuilder = null,
        ?AssertInstanceOfTypeMatcher $typeMatcher = null,
    ) {
        $this->methodNameResolver = $methodNameResolver ?? new CallMethodNameResolver();
        $this->argumentResolver = $argumentResolver ?? new CallArgumentResolver();
        $this->classStringResolver = $classStringResolver ?? new ClassStringExpressionResolver();
        $this->targetMatcher = $targetMatcher ?? new PhpUnitCallTargetMatcher();
        $this->errorBuilder = $errorBuilder ?? new NoRedundantAssertInstanceOfErrorBuilder();
        $this->typeMatcher = $typeMatcher ?? new AssertInstanceOfTypeMatcher();
    }

    /**
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function errors(\PhpParser\Node\Expr $node, Scope $scope): array
    {
        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Expr\MethodCall) {
            if (!$this->targetMatcher->isThisMethodCall($node)) {
                return [];
            }

            return $this->errorsForCall(
                $this->methodNameResolver->resolve($node->name),
                $node->args,
                $node->getStartLine(),
                $scope,
            );
        }

        if ($node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Expr\StaticCall) {
            if (!$this->targetMatcher->isStaticCallOnPhpUnitAssert($node, $scope)) {
                return [];
            }

            return $this->errorsForCall(
                $this->methodNameResolver->resolve($node->name),
                $node->args,
                $node->getStartLine(),
                $scope,
            );
        }

        return [];
    }

    /**
     * @param array<array-key, \PhpParser\Node\Arg|\PhpParser\Node\ArgPlaceholder|\PhpParser\Node\VariadicPlaceholder> $args
     * @return list<IdentifierRuleError>
     */
    public function errorsForCall(?string $methodName, array $args, int $line, Scope $scope): array
    {
        if ($methodName !== 'assertInstanceOf') {
            return [];
        }

        $expectedExpression = $this->argumentResolver->valueAt($args, 0);
        $actualExpression = $this->argumentResolver->valueAt($args, 1);
        if ($expectedExpression === null || $actualExpression === null) {
            return [];
        }

        $expectedTypeName = $this->classStringResolver->resolve($expectedExpression, $scope);
        if ($expectedTypeName === null) {
            return [];
        }

        $actualType = $scope->getType($actualExpression);
        $actualTypeNames = $actualType->getObjectClassNames();
        if (count($actualTypeNames) !== 1) {
            return [];
        }

        if (!$this->typeMatcher->matches($expectedTypeName, $actualType, $actualTypeNames[0])) {
            return [];
        }

        return [$this->errorBuilder->build($actualTypeNames[0], $expectedTypeName, $line)];
    }
}

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/toolkit-rector-docs.py <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
root=Path('/Users/ab/Projects/php-ai-toolkit/packages/phpstan-guard-rules')
safe={
'ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule': 'Expands single-line PHPDoc on named class-like declarations and public methods, properties, and constants. Annotation contents are retained. Anonymous classes and non-public members are unchanged.',
'OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule': 'Adds `#[\\Override]` using the same parent-method checks as the PHPStan rule. Constructors, private or abstract parent methods, interface-only implementations, and existing attributes are skipped. The attribute syntax works on PHP 8.0+; PHP validates the built-in attribute from 8.3.',
}
risky={
'ForbiddenCommentRule': 'Removes ordinary comments containing forbidden suppression directives and standalone suppression lines in PHPDoc. Other PHPDoc tags are preserved. Removing a suppression can expose PHPStan or Infection failures; review those failures instead of hiding them again. Ambiguous inline PHPDoc mentions remain for manual editing.',
'ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule': 'Replaces `$object->__toString()` with `(string) $object` and `$object->__invoke(...)` with `$object(...)`. Cast and invocation protocols can have different runtime behavior for unusual receivers. Other magic methods, static or nullsafe calls, first-class callables, and `__toString` calls with arguments are skipped.',
'ForbidNonDocCommentRule': 'Removes prohibited ordinary comments attached to parser nodes. It uses the PHPStan token-context policy to retain `//` comments in catches and array literals, all PHPDoc, and suppression comments handled by `ForbiddenCommentRector`. Comments may contain licensing information, tool instructions, or useful explanations: review every deletion. Comments not attached to a parser node need manual editing.',
'ForbidEmptyCatchRule': 'Adds `throw $caught;` to an empty catch with an existing variable. This makes a previously swallowed failure propagate and may stop the application. Choose logging or recovery manually when rethrowing is inappropriate. Non-empty catches and catches without a variable are unchanged.',
'RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule': 'Adds fully qualified `@throws` tags for specific escaping direct throws in methods, using the PHPStan rule’s catch and inheritance analysis. Existing tags are retained and duplicate missing types are added once. This changes the declared API and checked-exception analysis, so review callers. Generic `Exception`/`Throwable` throws are left for manual replacement with meaningful exception types.',
'RequireExceptionChainingRule': 'Adds the named `previous: $caught` argument to unchained throws of standard built-in exceptions, including SPL exceptions, with a known `message, code, previous` constructor. This changes the exception chain seen by handlers. Custom constructors, `ErrorException`, factory calls, unpacked arguments, existing previous arguments (even explicit `null`), unbound catches, and nested callables are skipped. Review the caught variable if the catch body reassigns it.',
'RequireListForArrayLiteralRule': 'Changes direct `array<int, V>` branches in `@var` or return tags to `list<V>` when the existing literal analysis proves a list initializer or list returns. PHPStan/Psalm variants, nullable types, and union/intersection branches are supported; nested value types and input parameters are preserved. This narrows a contract, so check later property writes and overriding implementations. Multi-property declarations and uncertain array expressions are skipped. PHPDoc formatting may be normalized.',
'ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule': 'Removes prose before the first annotation on restricted test classes and methods. Complete tags and continuation lines are retained; prose-only PHPDoc is removed. Descriptions may explain intent, so review their removal. Defaults to `Tests\\Unit` and `Tests\\Integration`; configure the same namespace prefixes as PHPStan when your project differs.',
}
manual={
'ForbidFileTermRule':'The replacement for a forbidden term depends on its meaning and location; deleting text can alter code, strings, or contracts.',
'ForbidDependencyRule':'Repair requires choosing an allowed dependency direction, moving responsibilities, or introducing a boundary. Removing a reference would discard behavior.',
'ForbiddenNamespaceRule':'A replacement namespace and all external references, autoload mappings, and configuration must be chosen together.',
'SrcUnitTestPairRule':'A meaningful test must assert intended behavior. Generating an empty matching file would only hide the violation.',
'RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule':'The API description and contract require knowledge of intended behavior. Placeholder documentation does not satisfy the policy’s purpose.',
'RequireExampleOnPublicApiRule':'An executable example needs meaningful input, output, and side-effect expectations that cannot be inferred reliably.',
'EnforceVisibilityScopeRule':'Changing visibility annotations or moving consumers requires an API ownership decision; automatically widening visibility would conceal the boundary violation.',
'EnforceMutationContractRule':'The author must decide whether to remove a side effect or declare it, including effects allowed by inherited contracts. Automatically declaring every mutation would legitimize unintended behavior.',
'ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule':'A domain-specific replacement name and updates to dynamic references and configuration require project knowledge.',
'NoNonPublicMethodRule':'Choose whether to extract a collaborator, inline behavior, or make it a deliberate public API. Merely widening method visibility does not implement this design policy.',
'ForbidBroadCatchRule':'The appropriate exception types and recovery policy depend on what the boundary is intended to handle. Narrowing or deleting the catch can change failure handling.',
'ForbidGenericThrowsTagRule':'Choose the actual specific exception contract. Removing a generic tag or guessing a type can make exception analysis unsound.',
'ForbidInternalMixedTypeRule':'Determine and validate the actual type or deliberately expose a public boundary. Deleting `mixed` or guessing a narrower type is not a repair.',
'RequireExhaustiveDispatchRule':'Each missing enum, literal, or sealed-class branch needs a meaningful result. Inventing a throw/default branch can discard business behavior; removing a default may change future or out-of-contract behavior. This also covers the internal `RequireExhaustiveClassDispatchRule` implementation.',
'NoPropertyInTestClassRule':'Moving shared state into test-local setup requires preserving fixtures, lifecycle hooks, and test isolation.',
'NoClassConstantInTestClassRule':'Choose whether each constant belongs in a local value or provider; preserve its references and intended test data.',
'NoPrivateMethodInTestClassRule':'Inline the behavior or extract a tested collaborator. Changing visibility alone would leave a prohibited helper.',
'NoHelperMethodInTestClassRule':'Helper extraction or inlining requires deciding what the test should exercise and keeping the assertions intact.',
'NoControlFlowInTestMethodRule':'Split scenarios into independent tests or providers with meaningful expected values; mechanical branch removal loses coverage.',
'NoTraitUseInTestClassRule':'Trait state, hooks, aliases, and precedence must be resolved when inlining or extracting behavior.',
'NoReflectionInTestClassRule':'Replace reflection with observable public behavior or a deliberate integration boundary. That requires redesigning the test.',
'NoRedundantAssertInstanceOfRule':'Replace the redundant assertion with a meaningful behavioral assertion. Deleting it can remove argument side effects or leave a test with no assertions.',
'NoBrokenCodeExpectationRule':'Fix the production defect and assert intended behavior instead of substituting an arbitrary exception class.',
'PhpUnitMockApiRule':'Selecting an interface, real collaborator, mock, or stub depends on the test contract and expected interactions.',
'TestNamingConventionRule':'Method and provider names must describe the scenario, and references in annotations, attributes, configuration, and filters must remain consistent.',
'ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule':'This legacy opt-in rule requires choosing a concrete value union, shape, or domain type. Guessing the return contract would be unsafe.',
}
assert not (set(safe)&set(risky))
for file in sorted((root/'docs/rules').glob('*.md')):
 name=file.stem
 assert name in safe or name in risky or name in manual,name
 kind='Safe' if name in safe else 'Risky' if name in risky else 'Unavailable'
 body=(safe|risky|manual)[name]
 text=file.read_text()
 lines=text.splitlines(); row=next(i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith('| Scope |'))
 lines.insert(row+1,f'| Rector | [{kind}](../rector.md) |')
 text='\n'.join(lines)+'\n'
 section='## Rector\n\n'
 if kind!='Unavailable':
  rector=name[:-4]+'Rector'
  section+=f'**{kind}** — [`Toolkit\\Rector\\{rector}`](../../src/Rector/{rector}.php), provided by `rector/{kind.lower()}.php`.\n\n'
 else: section+='**Unavailable** — no automatic transformation is provided.\n\n'
 section+=body+'\n\nSee [Rector setup and safety categories](../rector.md) for installation and execution.\n'
 text=text.rstrip()+'\n\n'+section
 file.write_text(text)
p=root/'docs/phpstan-rules.md';lines=p.read_text().splitlines()
for i,l in enumerate(lines):
 if l=='| Rule | Description | Error Identifier |': lines[i]=l+' Rector |'
 elif l=='|------|-------------|------------------|': lines[i]=l+'--------|'
 elif l.startswith('| [') and '(rules/' in l:
  name=l.split(']')[0][3:]
  kind='Safe' if name in safe else 'Risky' if name in risky else 'Unavailable'
  lines[i]=l+f' [{kind}](rules/{name}.md#rector) |'

+# Rector Support
+
+The package provides ten optional Rector rules: two safe transformations and

+risks, or reason automatic changes are unavailable.

+

+
+```sh

+installing this package does not require Rector. Projects retaining PHPStan 1
+must run Rector from a separate tool installation with this package installed.

+

+

+

+
+return RectorConfig::configure()
+    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
+    ->withSets([
+        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/safe.php',
+    ]);
+```
+
+Preview the changes, then apply them:
+

+vendor/bin/rector process
+```

+

+appropriate for your project:

# Rector Support

The package provides ten optional Rector rules: two safe transformations and
eight transformations that require review. Every PHPStan rule is classified in
the [rule list](phpstan-rules.md); each rule page explains its supported cases,
risks, or reason automatic changes are unavailable.

## Installation

Install Rector in the consuming project:

```sh
composer require --dev rector/rector:^2.6.7
```

The supported Rector runtime is `^2.6.7` with PHP 8.0 or later. Rector 2 requires
PHPStan 2. The PHPStan extension itself still supports `^1.12 || ^2.0`, and
installing this package does not require Rector. Projects retaining PHPStan 1
must run Rector from a separate tool installation with this package installed.

## Safe Changes

Create `rector.php` in your project:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withSets([
        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/safe.php',
    ]);
```

Preview the changes, then apply them:

```sh
vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run
vendor/bin/rector process
```

The safe set preserves executable behavior and documented contract contents in
the supported cases. It expands single-line public PHPDoc and adds `#[Override]`
where the existing PHPStan rule confirms a valid concrete parent override.
The new attribute is observable through reflection; projects that instantiate
attributes on PHP before 8.3 need an `Override` polyfill or can select only the
PHPDoc rule. Line-number-sensitive code or tools may observe formatting changes.

## Risky Changes

Risky rules can change runtime behavior, declared types or exceptions, test
documentation, or analysis suppressions. Their implementation is deliberately
limited to specific patterns, and they leave unsupported cases unchanged.
Review the diff and run PHPStan and the test suite after applying them.

Add the risky set explicitly alongside the safe set when those changes are
appropriate for your project:

```php
return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withSets([
        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/safe.php',
        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/risky.php',
    ]);
```

The risky set does not import the safe set, and the safe set never imports risky
rules. Neither set registers itself automatically through `rules.neon`.

| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md#rector) | `OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector` | Safe |
| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbidNonDocCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidEmptyCatchRule](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md#rector) | `ForbidEmptyCatchRector` | Risky |

## Selecting Individual Rules

Use `withRules()` to select individual transformations:

```php
use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\RequireExceptionChainingRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        RequireExceptionChainingRector::class,
    ]);
```

Rector does not read `parameters.toolkit` from `phpstan.neon`. Keep the selected
rules, paths, skips, and test namespace prefixes aligned with your PHPStan policy.
For custom restricted test namespaces, configure the prose-removal rule:

```php
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withConfiguredRule(ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector::class, [
        'Project\Tests\Unit',
        'Project\Tests\Integration',
    ]);
```

## Unavailable Changes

Rules classified as unavailable require decisions about domain types, public
APIs, dependency ownership, test scenarios, or meaningful assertions. The package
does not invent examples, remove assertions, widen visibility, or add arbitrary
dispatch branches to make those diagnostics disappear. Follow the manual repair
instructions on the corresponding rule page.

## Verification

The unit suite runs the real Rector CLI against before/after fixtures for every
provided transformation. It checks unchanged unsupported cases and runs Rector
again in dry-run mode to detect non-idempotent changes. Run it from the package:

```sh
composer test:unit -- --filter Rector
```

See the upstream [custom rule documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/custom-rule)
and [set documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/sets) for Rector configuration concepts.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared;

use PHPStan\Analyser\Scope;

/**
 * Detects anonymous class-like nodes for PHPDoc rules.
 */
final class AnonymousClassDetector
{
    /**
     * Reports whether the class-like node represents an anonymous class.
     */
    public function isAnonymous(\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike $node, Scope $scope): bool
    {
        if (!$node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Class_) {
            return false;
        }

        if ($node->name === null) {
            return true;
        }

        $classReflection = $scope->getClassReflection();
        if ($classReflection !== null && $classReflection->isAnonymous()) {
            return true;
        }

        return str_starts_with($node->name->toString(), 'AnonymousClass');
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Toolkit\PhpStan\Rule\Shared;

use PHPStan\Analyser\Scope;

/**
 * Detects anonymous class-like nodes for PHPDoc rules.
 */
final class AnonymousClassDetector
{
    /**
     * Reports whether the class-like node represents an anonymous class.
     */
    public function isAnonymous(\PhpParser\Node\Stmt\ClassLike $node, Scope $scope): bool
    {
        if (!$node instanceof \PhpParser\Node\Stmt\Class_) {
            return false;
        }

        if ($node->name === null) {
            return true;
        }

        $classReflection = $scope->getClassReflection();
        if ($classReflection !== null && $classReflection->isAnonymous()) {
            return true;
        }

        return str_starts_with($node->name->toString(), 'AnonymousClass');
    }
}
"}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Tests\Unit\Rector;

use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\CoversClass;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Large;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
use Tests\Rector\RectorFixtureRunner;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidNonDocCommentRector;

/**
 * @covers \Toolkit\Rector\ForbidNonDocCommentRector
 * @large
 */
#[CoversClass(ForbidNonDocCommentRector::class)]
#[Large]
final class ForbidNonDocCommentRectorTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testRefactorPreservesUnsupportedCasesAndIsIdempotent(): void
    {
        $result = (new RectorFixtureRunner())->run('ForbidNonDocCommentRector', 'ForbidNonDocCommentRector');
        self::assertSame(0, $result['exitCode'], $result['output']);
        self::assertSame($result['expected'], $result['actual']);
        self::assertTrue($result['idempotent'], 'A second Rector run must have no diff.');
    }

    public function testGetNodeTypesRegistersNodesAndRejectsUnrelatedInput(): void
    {
        $rule = new ForbidNonDocCommentRector();
        self::assertNotEmpty($rule->getNodeTypes());
        self::assertNull($rule->refactor(new \PhpParser\Node\Expr\Variable('unrelated')));
    }

    public function testForbiddenOffsetsDistinguishesCommentsOnTheSameLine(): void
    {
        $source = '<?php $a = [/* forbidden */ 1]; /* also forbidden */';
        $offsets = (new ForbidNonDocCommentRector())->forbiddenOffsets($source);
        self::assertCount(2, $offsets);
        self::assertArrayHasKey(12, $offsets);
        self::assertArrayHasKey(31, $offsets);
    }
}

/**

 */
final class PublicMethodTestCoverageErrorBuilder
{
    /**
     * Builds an error for a public method with no matching test method prefix.
     */
    public function build(string $methodName, string $expectedPrefix, int $line): IdentifierRuleError
    {
        return RuleErrorBuilder::message(

                $expectedPrefix,
                $methodName
            )
        )
            ->identifier('customRules.publicMethodWithoutTest')

    }

L71: # Custom Rule
L72: 
L73: First, make sure it's not covered by cite2†any existing Rectors . Let's say we want to change method calls from `set*` to `change*`.
L74: 
L75:     `<?php
L76: 
L77:     $user = new User();
L78:     -$user->setPassword('123456');
L79:     +$user->changePassword('123456');
L80:     `
L81: ## 1. Create a New Rector and Implement Methodscite30†# L82: Create a class that extends cite31†`Rector\Rector\AbstractRector`†github.com . It will inherit useful methods e.g. to check node type and name. See the source (or type `$this->` in an IDE) for a list of available methods.
L83: 
L84:     `<?php
L85: 
L86:     namespace Utils\Rector\Rector;
L87: 
L88:     use PhpParser\Node;
L89:     use PhpParser\Node\Identifier;
L90:     use PhpParser\Node\Expr\MethodCall;
L91:     use Rector\Rector\AbstractRector;
L92: 
L93:     final class MyFirstRector extends AbstractRector
L94:     {
L95:         /**
L96:          * @return array<class-string<Node>>
L97:          */
L98:         public function getNodeTypes(): array
L99:         {
L100:             // what node types are we looking for?
L101:             // pick from
L102:             // https://github.com/rectorphp/php-parser-nodes-docs/
L103:             return [MethodCall::class];
L104:         }
L105: 
L106:         /**
L107:          * @param MethodCall $node
L108:          */
L109:         public function refactor(Node $node): ?Node
L110:         {
L111:             $methodCallName = $this->getName($node->name);
L112:             if ($methodCallName === null) {
L113:                 return null;
L114:             }
L115: 
L116:             // we only care about "set*" method names
L117:             if (! str_starts_with($methodCallName, 'set')) {
L118:                 // return null to skip it
L119:                 return null;
L120:             }
L121: 
L122:             $newMethodCallName = preg_replace(
L123:                 '#^set#', 'change', $methodCallName
L124:             );
L125: 
L126:             $node->name = new Identifier($newMethodCallName);
L127:             // return $node if you modified it
L128:             return $node;
L129:         }
L130:     }
L131:     `
L132: ## 2. File Structurecite32†# L133: This is how the file structure for custom rule in your own project will look like:
L134: 
L135:     `/src
L136:         SomeCode.php
L137: 
L138:     /utils
L139:         /rector
L140:             /src
L141:                 /Rector
L142:                     MyFirstRector.php
L143: 
L144:             /tests
L145:                 /Rector
L146:                     /MyFirstRector
L147:                         /Fixture
L148:                             test_fixture.php.inc
L149:                         /config
L150:                             config.php
L151:                         MyFirstRectorTest.php
L152: 
L153:     rector.php
L154:     composer.json
L155:     `
L156: ### Update `composer.json`cite33†# L157: 
L158: We also need to load Rector rules in `composer.json`:
L159: 
L160:     `{
L161:         "autoload": {
L162:             "psr-4": {
L163:                 "App\\": "src"
L164:             }
L165:         },
L166:         "autoload-dev": {
L167:             "psr-4": {
L168:                 "Utils\\Rector\\": "utils/rector/src",
L169:                 "Utils\\Rector\\Tests\\": "utils/rector/tests"
L170:             }
L171:         }
L172:     }
L173:     `
L174: After adding this to `composer.json`, be sure to reload Composer's class map:
L175: 
L176:     `composer dump-autoload
L177:     `
L178: ## 3. Register Itcite34†# L179: 
L180:     `<?php
L181: 
L182:     use Utils\Rector\Rector\MyFirstRector;
L183:     use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
L184: 
L185:     return RectorConfig::configure()
L186:         ->withRules([
L187:             MyFirstRector::class
L188:         ]);
L189:     `
L190: 
L191: ## 4. Let Rector Refactor Your Codecite35†# L192: 
L193: The `rector.php` configuration is loaded by default, so we can skip it.
L194: 
L195:     `# see the diff first
L196:     vendor/bin/rector process src --dry-run
L197: 
L198:     # if it's ok, apply
L199:     vendor/bin/rector process src
L200:     `
L201: 
L202: That's it!
L203: ## 5. Write a Testcite36†# L204: 
L205: Writing a test for your custom rule will save you a lot of time in future debugging. Rector provides a structured way of running your rule on different snippets of code, so you can validate it works as expected in a variety of cases.
L206: 
L207: There are 2 composer packages needed to run tests for your custom rule:
L208: 
L209:   * `phpunit/phpunit`: the testing framework
L210:   * `rector/rector`: this contains the `AbstractRectorTestCase` class to simplify test configuration
L211: ### MyFirstRectorTest.phpcite37†# L212: This class handles the heavy lifting of preparing Rector & running it against your test cases. The usual structure of the test class is as follows:
L213: 
L214:     `<?php
L215: 
L216:     declare(strict_types=1);
L217: 
L218:     namespace Utils\Rector\Tests\Rector\MyFirstRector;
L219: 
L220:     use Iterator;
L221:     use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
L222:     use Rector\Testing\PHPUnit\AbstractRectorTestCase;
L223: 
L224:     final class MyFirstRectorTest extends AbstractRectorTestCase
L225:     {
L226:         #[DataProvider('provideData')]
L227:         public function test(string $filePath): void
L228:         {
L229:             $this->doTestFile($filePath);
L230:         }
L231: 
L232:         public static function provideData(): Iterator
L233:         {
L234:             return self::yieldFilesFromDirectory(__DIR__ . '/Fixture');
L235:         }
L236: 
L237:         public function provideConfigFilePath(): string
L238:         {
L239:             return __DIR__ . '/config/config.php';
L240:         }
L241:     }
L242:     `
L243: There are 3 methods in this test class:
L244:   * `public function test(string $filePath): void`:
L245:     * This method helps PHPUnit detect the test
L246:     * For `$filePath`, we use a cite38†PHPUnit DataProvider†docs.phpunit.de L247:     * This triggers a run for every test file in your `Fixture` directory
L248:   * `public static function provideData(): Iterator`:
L249:     * Using `self::yieldFilesFromDirectory` it iterates over all test cases you provided
L250:     * By default this only picks up files ending on `.php.inc`
L251:   * `public function provideConfigFilePath(): string`:
L252:     * Returns a `rector.php`-styled file configuring the minimal set of rules needed to run the tests (including `MyFirstRector`)
L253: ### config/config.phpcite39†# L254: 
L255: This is a `rector.php`-styled file. If your rule is not configurable, it will look like this:
L256: 
L257:     `use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
L258:     use Utils\Rector\Rector\MyFirstRector;
L259: 
L260:     return RectorConfig::configure()
L261:         ->withRules([
L262:             MyFirstRector::class,
L263:         ]);
L264:     `
L265: 
L266: This essentially reflects how you would use your rule in real life.
L267: ### Fixture/*.php.inccite40†# L268: 
L269: These are the snippets of code on which Rector runs your custom rule. To prevent automated tools from picking up those snippets, add an extra suffix `.inc` (so `example.php` becomes `example.php.inc`).
L270: 
L271: There are two options for every test file: either the snippet should be changed by your rule, or it should stay the same.
L272: #### Fixture/test_fixture.php.inccite41†# L273: Assuming your rule changes `$user->setPassword('123456')` to `$user->changePassword('123456')`, this is an example snippet:
L274: 
L275:     `<?php
L276: 
L277:     namespace Utils\Rector\Tests\Rector\MyFirstRector\Fixture;
L278: 
L279:     class SomeClass
L280:     {
L281:         public function handlePasswordChange(User $user, string $password)
L282:         {
L283:             $user->setPassword($password);
L284:         }
L285:     }
L286: 
L287:     ?>
L288:     -----
L289:     <?php
L290: 
L291:     namespace Utils\Rector\Tests\Rector\MyFirstRector\Fixture;
L292: 
L293:     class SomeClass
L294:     {
L295:         public function handlePasswordChange(User $user, string $password)
L296:         {
L297:             $user->changePassword($password);
L298:         }
L299:     }
L300: 
L301:     ?>
L302:     `
L303: This file contains a "before" and "after" situation, separated by exactly 5 dashes: `-----`. The `AbstractRectorTestCase` detects the `-----`, runs the rules configured in `config/config.php` on the snippet before the `-----` and asserts that the changed file exactly matches the snippet after the `-----`.
L304: #### Fixture/skip_rule_test_fixture.php.inccite42†# L305: 
L306: There are cases where you want to check that your rule is not applied. The file structure is very similar to `Fixture/test_fixture.php.inc` with 1 exception: it only contains a "before" situation.
L307: It is not necessary to prefix the fixture with `skip`, but doing so makes it easy to see that no changes are expected.
L308: 
L309:     `<?php
L310: 
L311:     namespace Utils\Rector\Tests\Rector\MyFirstRector\Fixture;
L312: 
L313:     class SomeClass
L314:     {
L315:         public function handleLogin(User $user, string $password)
L316:         {
L317:             return $user->isCorrectPassword($password);
L318:         }
L319:     }
L320: 
L321:     ?>
L322:     `
L323: There is no `-----`, so `AbstractRectorTestCase` runs the rules on the snippet and asserts that no changes are applied.
L324: ### Running Your Testscite43†# L325: 
L326:     `vendor/bin/phpunit tests
L327:     `

AGENTS.md
# Rector Support

The package provides ten optional Rector rules: two safe transformations and
eight transformations that require review. Every PHPStan rule is classified in
the [rule list](phpstan-rules.md); each rule page explains its supported cases,
risks, or reason automatic changes are unavailable.

## Installation

Install Rector in the consuming project:

```sh
composer require --dev rector/rector:^2.6.7
```

The supported Rector runtime is `^2.6.7` with PHP 8.0 or later. Rector 2 requires
PHPStan 2. The PHPStan extension itself still supports `^1.12 || ^2.0`, and
installing this package does not require Rector. Projects retaining PHPStan 1
must run Rector from a separate tool installation with this package installed.

## Safe Changes

Create `rector.php` in your project:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withSets([
        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/safe.php',
    ]);
```

Preview the changes, then apply them:

```sh
vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run
vendor/bin/rector process
```

The safe set preserves executable behavior and documented contract contents in
the supported cases. It expands single-line public PHPDoc and adds `#[Override]`
where the existing PHPStan rule confirms a valid concrete parent override.
The new attribute is observable through reflection; projects that instantiate
attributes on PHP before 8.3 need an `Override` polyfill or can select only the
PHPDoc rule. Line-number-sensitive code or tools may observe formatting changes.

## Risky Changes

Risky rules can change runtime behavior, declared types or exceptions, test
documentation, or analysis suppressions. Their implementation is deliberately
limited to specific patterns, and they leave unsupported cases unchanged.
Review the diff and run PHPStan and the test suite after applying them.

Add the risky set explicitly alongside the safe set when those changes are
appropriate for your project:

```php
return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withSets([
        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/safe.php',
        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/risky.php',
    ]);
```

The risky set does not import the safe set, and the safe set never imports risky
rules. Neither set registers itself automatically through `rules.neon`.

| PHPStan rule | Rector class in `Toolkit\Rector` | Category |
|-------------|----------------------------------|----------|
| [ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md#rector) | `ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector` | Safe |
| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md#rector) | `OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector` | Safe |
| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbidNonDocCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidEmptyCatchRule](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md#rector) | `ForbidEmptyCatchRector` | Risky |
| [RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule](rules/RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule.md#rector) | `RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRector` | Risky |
| [RequireExceptionChainingRule](rules/RequireExceptionChainingRule.md#rector) | `RequireExceptionChainingRector` | Risky |
| [RequireListForArrayLiteralRule](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md#rector) | `RequireListForArrayLiteralRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule](rules/ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule.md#rector) | `ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector` | Risky |

## Selecting Individual Rules

Use `withRules()` to select individual transformations:

```php
use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\RequireExceptionChainingRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        RequireExceptionChainingRector::class,
    ]);
```

Rector does not read `parameters.toolkit` from `phpstan.neon`. Keep the selected
rules, paths, skips, and test namespace prefixes aligned with your PHPStan policy.
For custom restricted test namespaces, configure the prose-removal rule:

```php
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withConfiguredRule(ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector::class, [
        'Project\Tests\Unit',
        'Project\Tests\Integration',
    ]);
```

## Unavailable Changes

Rules classified as unavailable require decisions about domain types, public
APIs, dependency ownership, test scenarios, or meaningful assertions. The package
does not invent examples, remove assertions, widen visibility, or add arbitrary
dispatch branches to make those diagnostics disappear. Follow the manual repair
instructions on the corresponding rule page.

## Verification

The unit suite runs the real Rector CLI against before/after fixtures for every
provided transformation. It checks unchanged unsupported cases and runs Rector
again in dry-run mode to detect non-idempotent changes. Run it from the package:

```sh
composer test:unit -- --filter Rector
```

See the upstream [custom rule documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/custom-rule)
and [set documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/set-lists) for Rector configuration concepts.
# phpstan-guard-rules

[![PHP](https://img.shields.io/badge/php-8.0%2B-777bb4?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://www.php.net/)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](../../LICENSE)

Strict PHPStan rules for AI-assisted PHP development, covering production code,
public API contracts, and test design.
Part of [php-ai-toolkit](../../README.md).

## Requirements

- PHP 8.0 or later.
- PHPStan `^1.12 || ^2.0`.
- Composer.

## Installation

From a local checkout, register the packages in the consuming project:

```sh
composer config repositories.php-ai-toolkit path '../php-ai-toolkit/packages/*'
composer config minimum-stability dev
composer config prefer-stable true
composer require --dev k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules:dev-main
```

Adjust the checkout path for your project.

## Usage

Include the shipped rules and PHPStan's strict rules in `phpstan.neon`:

```neon
includes:
    - vendor/phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules/rules.neon
    - vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rules.neon

parameters:
    level: max
    paths:
        - src
        - tests
```

Adjust the analysis paths to your project, then run `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`.
If `phpstan/extension-installer` already loads these files, avoid including them twice.

Optional [Rector support](docs/rector.md) provides separate safe and risky sets.
Install `rector/rector:^2.6.7`, import `rector/safe.php` from this package in your
Rector configuration, and preview changes with `vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run`.
Select `rector/risky.php` explicitly for changes that require behavioral or contract
review. The rule reference records automatic-fix availability for every rule.

## Documentation

The [rule reference](docs/phpstan-rules.md) lists identifiers, configuration,
Rector safety categories, and links to each rule. The [PHPStan setup skill](skills/setup-toolkit-phpstan/SKILL.md)
also configures the separate AI formatter.

# Documentation Lookup

Retrieve current documentation and code examples for any library using the Context7 CLI.

Run commands with `npx ctx7@latest` so setup always uses the latest CLI without a global install:

```bash
npx ctx7@latest library <name> "<query>"
npx ctx7@latest docs <libraryId> "<query>"
```

Optionally install globally if you prefer a bare `ctx7` command:

```bash
npm install -g ctx7@latest
```

## Workflow

Two-step process: resolve the library name to an ID, then query docs with that ID.

```bash
# Step 1: Resolve library ID
npx ctx7@latest library <name> "<query>"

# Step 2: Query documentation
npx ctx7@latest docs <libraryId> "<query>"
```

You MUST call `library` first to obtain a valid library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format `/org/project` or `/org/project/version`.

IMPORTANT: Do not run these commands more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 attempts, use the best result you have.

## Step 1: Resolve a Library

Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

```bash
npx ctx7@latest library React "How to clean up useEffect with async operations"
npx ctx7@latest library "Next.js" "How to set up app router with middleware"
npx ctx7@latest library Prisma "How to define one-to-many relations with cascade delete"
```

Use the official library name with proper punctuation (e.g., "Next.js" not "nextjs", "Customer.io" not "customerio", "Three.js" not "threejs"). If results look wrong, try alternate spellings such as `next.js` before changing the query.

Always pass a `query` argument — it is required and directly affects result ranking. Use the user's intent to form the query, which helps disambiguate when multiple libraries share a similar name. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

### Result fields

Each result includes:

- **Library ID** — Context7-compatible identifier (format: `/org/project`)
- **Name** — Library or package name
- **Description** — Short summary
- **Code Snippets** — Number of available code examples
- **Source Reputation** — Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- **Benchmark Score** — Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- **Versions** — List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format is `/org/project/version`.

### Selection process

1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Select the most relevant match based on:
   - Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
   - Description relevance to the query's intent
   - Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
   - Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
   - Benchmark score (higher is better, 100 is the maximum)
3. If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
4. If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements
5. For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match

### Version-specific IDs

If the user mentions a specific version, use a version-specific library ID:

```bash
# General (latest indexed)
npx ctx7@latest docs /vercel/next.js "How to set up app router"

# Version-specific
npx ctx7@latest docs /vercel/next.js/v14.3.0-canary.87 "How to set up app router"
```

The available versions are listed in the `library` command output. Use the closest match to what the user specified.

## Step 2: Query Documentation

Retrieves up-to-date documentation and code examples for the resolved library.

```bash
npx ctx7@latest docs /facebook/react "How to clean up useEffect with async operations"
npx ctx7@latest docs /vercel/next.js "How to add authentication middleware to app router"
npx ctx7@latest docs /prisma/prisma "How to define one-to-many relations with cascade delete"
```

If you know the programming language the user writes in, add `--language` so code examples in that language rank first:

```bash
npx ctx7@latest docs /websites/twilio "How to send an SMS" --language Ruby
```

### Writing good queries

The query directly affects the quality of results. Be specific and include relevant details, but keep each query to one topic — if the question spans multiple distinct concepts, run a separate `docs` command per concept instead of combining them, unless the question is about how the concepts interact. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

| Quality | Example |
|---------|---------|
| Good | `"How to set up authentication with JWT in Express.js"` |
| Good | `"React useEffect cleanup function with async operations"` |
| Bad (too vague) | `"auth"` |
| Bad (too vague) | `"hooks"` |
| Bad (too broad) | `"routing and auth and caching in Next.js"` |

Describe what to look up in the library's documentation, rather than the task to complete — vague one-word queries return generic results, and multi-topic queries dilute ranking and return shallow results for each topic.

The output contains two types of content: **code snippets** (titled, with language-tagged blocks) and **info snippets** (prose explanations with breadcrumb context).

## Authentication

Works without authentication. For higher rate limits:

```bash
# Option A: environment variable
export CONTEXT7_API_KEY=your_key

# Option B: OAuth login
npx ctx7@latest login
```

## Error Handling

If a command fails with a quota error ("Monthly quota reached" or "quota exceeded"):
1. Inform the user their Context7 quota is exhausted
2. Suggest they authenticate for higher limits: `npx ctx7@latest login`
3. If they cannot or choose not to authenticate, answer from training knowledge and clearly note it may be outdated

Do not silently fall back to training data — always tell the user why Context7 was not used.

## Common Mistakes

- Library IDs require a `/` prefix — `/facebook/react` not `facebook/react`
- Always run `npx ctx7@latest library` first — `npx ctx7@latest docs react "hooks"` will fail without a valid ID
- Use descriptive queries, not single words — `"React useEffect cleanup function"` not `"hooks"`
- One topic per query — split `"routing and auth and caching"` into a separate `docs` command per concept, unless the question is about how they interact
- Do not include sensitive information (API keys, passwords, credentials) in queries
