# Rector Support

The package provides ten optional Rector rules: two safe transformations and
eight transformations that require review. Every PHPStan rule is classified in
the [rule list](phpstan-rules.md); each rule page explains its supported cases,
risks, or reason automatic changes are unavailable.

## Installation

Install Rector in the consuming project:

```sh
composer require --dev rector/rector:^2.6.7
```

The supported Rector runtime is `^2.6.7` with PHP 8.0 or later. Rector 2 requires
PHPStan 2. The PHPStan extension itself still supports `^1.12 || ^2.0`, and
installing this package does not require Rector. Projects retaining PHPStan 1
must run Rector from a separate tool installation with this package installed.

## Safe Changes

Create `rector.php` in your project:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withSets([
        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/safe.php',
    ]);
```

Preview the changes, then apply them:

```sh
vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run
vendor/bin/rector process
```

The safe set preserves executable behavior and documented contract contents in
the supported cases. It expands single-line public PHPDoc and adds `#[Override]`
where the existing PHPStan rule confirms a valid concrete parent override.
The new attribute is observable through reflection; projects that instantiate
attributes on PHP before 8.3 need an `Override` polyfill or can select only the
PHPDoc rule. Line-number-sensitive code or tools may observe formatting changes.

## Risky Changes

Risky rules can change runtime behavior, declared types or exceptions, test
documentation, or analysis suppressions. Their implementation is deliberately
limited to specific patterns, and they leave unsupported cases unchanged.
Review the diff and run PHPStan and the test suite after applying them.

Add the risky set explicitly alongside the safe set when those changes are
appropriate for your project:

```php
return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withSets([
        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/safe.php',
        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/risky.php',
    ]);
```

The risky set does not import the safe set, and the safe set never imports risky
rules. Neither set registers itself automatically through `rules.neon`.

| PHPStan rule | Rector class in `Toolkit\Rector` | Category |
|-------------|----------------------------------|----------|
| [ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md#rector) | `ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector` | Safe |
| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md#rector) | `OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector` | Safe |
| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbidNonDocCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidEmptyCatchRule](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md#rector) | `ForbidEmptyCatchRector` | Risky |
| [RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule](rules/RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule.md#rector) | `RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRector` | Risky |
| [RequireExceptionChainingRule](rules/RequireExceptionChainingRule.md#rector) | `RequireExceptionChainingRector` | Risky |
| [RequireListForArrayLiteralRule](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md#rector) | `RequireListForArrayLiteralRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule](rules/ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule.md#rector) | `ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector` | Risky |

## Selecting Individual Rules

Use `withRules()` to select individual transformations:

```php
use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\RequireExceptionChainingRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        RequireExceptionChainingRector::class,
    ]);
```

Rector does not read `parameters.toolkit` from `phpstan.neon`. Keep the selected
rules, paths, skips, and test namespace prefixes aligned with your PHPStan policy.
For custom restricted test namespaces, configure the prose-removal rule:

```php
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withConfiguredRule(ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector::class, [
        'Project\Tests\Unit',
        'Project\Tests\Integration',
    ]);
```

## Unavailable Changes

Rules classified as unavailable require decisions about domain types, public
APIs, dependency ownership, test scenarios, or meaningful assertions. The package
does not invent examples, remove assertions, widen visibility, or add arbitrary
dispatch branches to make those diagnostics disappear. Follow the manual repair
instructions on the corresponding rule page.

## Verification

The unit suite runs the real Rector CLI against before/after fixtures for every
provided transformation. It checks unchanged unsupported cases and runs Rector
again in dry-run mode to detect non-idempotent changes. Run it from the package:

```sh
composer test:unit -- --filter Rector
```

See the upstream [custom rule documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/custom-rule)
and [set documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/set-lists) for Rector configuration concepts.
# phpstan-guard-rules

[![PHP](https://img.shields.io/badge/php-8.0%2B-777bb4?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://www.php.net/)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](../../LICENSE)

Strict PHPStan rules for AI-assisted PHP development, covering production code,
public API contracts, and test design.
Part of [php-ai-toolkit](../../README.md).

## Requirements

- PHP 8.0 or later.
- PHPStan `^1.12 || ^2.0`.
- Composer.

## Installation

From a local checkout, register the packages in the consuming project:

```sh
composer config repositories.php-ai-toolkit path '../php-ai-toolkit/packages/*'
composer config minimum-stability dev
composer config prefer-stable true
composer require --dev k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules:dev-main
```

Adjust the checkout path for your project.

## Usage

Include the shipped rules and PHPStan's strict rules in `phpstan.neon`:

```neon
includes:
    - vendor/phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules/rules.neon
    - vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rules.neon

parameters:
    level: max
    paths:
        - src
        - tests
```

Adjust the analysis paths to your project, then run `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`.
If `phpstan/extension-installer` already loads these files, avoid including them twice.

Optional [Rector support](docs/rector.md) provides separate safe and risky sets.
Install `rector/rector:^2.6.7`, import `rector/safe.php` from this package in your
Rector configuration, and preview changes with `vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run`.
Select `rector/risky.php` explicitly for changes that require behavioral or contract
review. The rule reference records automatic-fix availability for every rule.

## Documentation

The [rule reference](docs/phpstan-rules.md) lists identifiers, configuration,
Rector safety categories, and links to each rule. The [PHPStan setup skill](skills/setup-toolkit-phpstan/SKILL.md)
also configures the separate AI formatter.

# Documentation Lookup

Retrieve current documentation and code examples for any library using the Context7 CLI.

Run commands with `npx ctx7@latest` so setup always uses the latest CLI without a global install:

```bash
npx ctx7@latest library <name> "<query>"
npx ctx7@latest docs <libraryId> "<query>"
```

Optionally install globally if you prefer a bare `ctx7` command:

```bash
npm install -g ctx7@latest
```

## Workflow

Two-step process: resolve the library name to an ID, then query docs with that ID.

```bash
# Step 1: Resolve library ID
npx ctx7@latest library <name> "<query>"

# Step 2: Query documentation
npx ctx7@latest docs <libraryId> "<query>"
```

You MUST call `library` first to obtain a valid library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format `/org/project` or `/org/project/version`.

IMPORTANT: Do not run these commands more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 attempts, use the best result you have.

## Step 1: Resolve a Library

Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

```bash
npx ctx7@latest library React "How to clean up useEffect with async operations"
npx ctx7@latest library "Next.js" "How to set up app router with middleware"
npx ctx7@latest library Prisma "How to define one-to-many relations with cascade delete"
```

Use the official library name with proper punctuation (e.g., "Next.js" not "nextjs", "Customer.io" not "customerio", "Three.js" not "threejs"). If results look wrong, try alternate spellings such as `next.js` before changing the query.

Always pass a `query` argument — it is required and directly affects result ranking. Use the user's intent to form the query, which helps disambiguate when multiple libraries share a similar name. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

### Result fields

Each result includes:

- **Library ID** — Context7-compatible identifier (format: `/org/project`)
- **Name** — Library or package name
- **Description** — Short summary
- **Code Snippets** — Number of available code examples
- **Source Reputation** — Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- **Benchmark Score** — Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- **Versions** — List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format is `/org/project/version`.

### Selection process

1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Select the most relevant match based on:
   - Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
   - Description relevance to the query's intent
   - Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
   - Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
   - Benchmark score (higher is better, 100 is the maximum)
3. If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
4. If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements
5. For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match

### Version-specific IDs

If the user mentions a specific version, use a version-specific library ID:

```bash
# General (latest indexed)
npx ctx7@latest docs /vercel/next.js "How to set up app router"

# Version-specific
npx ctx7@latest docs /vercel/next.js/v14.3.0-canary.87 "How to set up app router"
```

The available versions are listed in the `library` command output. Use the closest match to what the user specified.

## Step 2: Query Documentation

Retrieves up-to-date documentation and code examples for the resolved library.

```bash
npx ctx7@latest docs /facebook/react "How to clean up useEffect with async operations"
npx ctx7@latest docs /vercel/next.js "How to add authentication middleware to app router"
npx ctx7@latest docs /prisma/prisma "How to define one-to-many relations with cascade delete"
```

If you know the programming language the user writes in, add `--language` so code examples in that language rank first:

```bash
npx ctx7@latest docs /websites/twilio "How to send an SMS" --language Ruby
```

### Writing good queries

The query directly affects the quality of results. Be specific and include relevant details, but keep each query to one topic — if the question spans multiple distinct concepts, run a separate `docs` command per concept instead of combining them, unless the question is about how the concepts interact. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

| Quality | Example |
|---------|---------|
| Good | `"How to set up authentication with JWT in Express.js"` |
| Good | `"React useEffect cleanup function with async operations"` |
| Bad (too vague) | `"auth"` |
| Bad (too vague) | `"hooks"` |
| Bad (too broad) | `"routing and auth and caching in Next.js"` |

Describe what to look up in the library's documentation, rather than the task to complete — vague one-word queries return generic results, and multi-topic queries dilute ranking and return shallow results for each topic.

The output contains two types of content: **code snippets** (titled, with language-tagged blocks) and **info snippets** (prose explanations with breadcrumb context).

## Authentication

Works without authentication. For higher rate limits:

```bash
# Option A: environment variable
export CONTEXT7_API_KEY=your_key

# Option B: OAuth login
npx ctx7@latest login
```

## Error Handling

If a command fails with a quota error ("Monthly quota reached" or "quota exceeded"):
1. Inform the user their Context7 quota is exhausted
2. Suggest they authenticate for higher limits: `npx ctx7@latest login`
3. If they cannot or choose not to authenticate, answer from training knowledge and clearly note it may be outdated

Do not silently fall back to training data — always tell the user why Context7 was not used.

## Common Mistakes

- Library IDs require a `/` prefix — `/facebook/react` not `facebook/react`
- Always run `npx ctx7@latest library` first — `npx ctx7@latest docs react "hooks"` will fail without a valid ID
- Use descriptive queries, not single words — `"React useEffect cleanup function"` not `"hooks"`
- One topic per query — split `"routing and auth and caching"` into a separate `docs` command per concept, unless the question is about how they interact
- Do not include sensitive information (API keys, passwords, credentials) in queries

# PHPStan Rules

Custom PHPStan rules provided by php-ai-toolkit. Each rule detects anti-patterns that actually occur in AI-generated code.

## Rector Support

Every rule below is classified as **Safe**, **Risky**, or **Unavailable** for automatic
changes. Safe and risky transformations are shipped as separate opt-in Rector sets.
A classification describes only the supported cases; each rule’s Rector section
lists skipped cases and review requirements. See [Rector setup](rector.md).

The legacy opt-in [ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule](rules/ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule.md#rector)
is also classified as **Unavailable**. Internal helper rules for mixed types and
class dispatch share their parent rule’s classification.

## General

Rules applied to all code.

| Rule | Description | Error Identifier | Rector |
|------|-------------|------------------|--------|
| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md) | Forbids `@phpstan-ignore` and `@infection-ignore-all` comments | `customRules.phpstanIgnoreComment`, `customRules.infectionIgnoreAllComment` | [Risky](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) |
| [ForbidFileTermRule](rules/ForbidFileTermRule.md) | Forbids configured literal terms in files matching restricted path patterns | `customRules.forbiddenFileTerm` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidFileTermRule.md#rector) |
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;

return static function (RectorConfig $config): void {
    $config->disableParallel();
    $config->phpVersion(80000);
    $cache = getenv('TOOLKIT_RECTOR_CACHE');
    if (is_string($cache) && $cache !== '') {
        $config->cacheDirectory($cache);
    }
    $set = getenv('TOOLKIT_RECTOR_SET');
    if (is_string($set) && $set !== '') {
        $config->sets([dirname(__DIR__, 2) . '/rector/' . $set . '.php']);
    } else {
        $config->rule('Toolkit\\Rector\\' . getenv('TOOLKIT_RECTOR_RULE'));
    }
};

# PHPStan Rules

Custom PHPStan rules provided by php-ai-toolkit. Each rule detects anti-patterns that actually occur in AI-generated code.

## Rector Support

Every rule below is classified as **Safe**, **Risky**, or **Unavailable** for automatic
changes. Enable the transformations you need by registering their Rector classes
with `withRules()` in `rector.php`.
A classification describes only the supported cases; each rule’s Rector section
lists skipped cases and review requirements. See [Rector setup](rector.md).

The legacy opt-in [ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule](rules/ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule.md#rector)
is also classified as **Unavailable**. Internal helper rules for mixed types and
class dispatch share their parent rule’s classification.

## General

```

Adjust the analysis paths to your project, then run `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`.
If `phpstan/extension-installer` already loads these files, avoid including them twice.

Optional [Rector support](docs/rector.md) provides safe and risky rule classes.
Install `rector/rector:^2.6.7` and select the rules in `rector.php`:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
    ]);
```

Preview changes with `vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run`. Add risky rule classes
only after reviewing their behavioral or contract changes. The rule reference
records automatic-fix availability for every rule.

## Documentation

The [rule reference](docs/phpstan.md) lists identifiers, configuration,
Rector safety categories, and links to each rule. The [PHPStan setup skill](skills/setup-toolkit-phpstan/SKILL.md)
also configures the separate AI formatter.

## License

[MIT](../../LICENSE)

The supported Rector runtime is `^2.6.7` with PHP 8.0 or later. Rector 2 requires
PHPStan 2. The PHPStan extension itself still supports `^1.12 || ^2.0`, and
installing this package does not require Rector. Projects retaining PHPStan 1
must run Rector from a separate tool installation with this package installed.

## Safe Changes

Create `rector.php` in your project:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
    ]);
```

Preview the changes, then apply them:

```sh
vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run
vendor/bin/rector process
```

These two rules preserve executable behavior and documented contract contents in
the supported cases. They expand single-line public PHPDoc and add `#[Override]`
where the existing PHPStan rule confirms a valid concrete parent override.
The new attribute is observable through reflection; projects that instantiate
attributes on PHP before 8.3 need an `Override` polyfill or can select only the
PHPDoc rule. Line-number-sensitive code or tools may observe formatting changes.

## Risky Changes

Risky rules can change runtime behavior, declared types or exceptions, test
documentation, or analysis suppressions. Their implementation is deliberately
limited to specific patterns, and they leave unsupported cases unchanged.
Review the diff and run PHPStan and the test suite after applying them.

Add individual risky rule classes after reviewing their supported cases. This
example enables exception chaining alongside the two safe rules:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\RequireExceptionChainingRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
        RequireExceptionChainingRector::class,
    ]);
```

Only the selected classes run. PHPStan's `rules.neon` does not register Rector
rules automatically.

## Rule Classes

| [RequireListForArrayLiteralRule](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md#rector) | `RequireListForArrayLiteralRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule](rules/ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule.md#rector) | `ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector` | Risky |

Rector does not read `parameters.toolkit` from `phpstan.neon`. Keep the selected

# AGENTS.md instructions for /Users/ab/Projects/php-ai-toolkit

<INSTRUCTIONS>
These AGENTS.md instructions replace all previously provided AGENTS.md instructions.

<!-- NOTE: You do not have permission to overwrite this file. Please ask a human operator to perform the changes for you. -->
# AGENTS

## Vision

Provide tools for AI-assisted PHP development that detect code, test, and configuration problems early and explain how to fix them. This repository is a monorepo of five Composer packages, each with its own dependencies and checks.

## Supported Versions

- **PHP**: 8.0 or later
- **PHPStan**: ^1.12 || ^2.0
- **PHPUnit**: ^9.6 || ^10.5 || ^11 || ^12 || ^13

## Architecture

| Package | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/guard-php` | Source, structure, documentation, and configuration policy checks and repairs. |
| `packages/docgen-php` | API documentation generation and site assets. |
| `packages/phpstan-guard-rules` | PHPStan rules and strict configuration. |
| `packages/phpunit-ai-reporter` | PHPUnit reporting, Doctest, and shared agent detection. |
| `packages/phpstan-ai-formatter` | PHPStan's `ai` error formatter. |

Run Composer commands in the owning package, for example
`composer --working-dir=packages/guard-php guard`. Each package provides `lint`,
`test`, and `test:unit` scripts. Check root documentation and structure with
`php packages/guard-php/bin/guard check --config=guard.yaml` after installing
Guard's dependencies.

### Branching Strategy

This project is developed on `main` only. Commit directly to `main`, whatever the size of the change.

- Do not create branches. A branch cannot be merged back here, so work left on one is stranded.
- Do not open pull requests. They are not part of this project's workflow.
- The common agent habit of branching before committing on a default branch does not apply here: `main` is the working branch.

### Rule Design Principles

- AI-friendly error messages: Every error message must clearly state *what is wrong* and *how to fix it*. An AI agent reading the message should be able to resolve the violation without additional context.
- Specific and identifiable: Messages must include enough detail (e.g., the offending symbol name, the expected pattern) so that each violation can be individually targeted in `ignoreErrors` configurations. Vague messages like "invalid code" are not acceptable.

## Documents

The root README follows Guard's monorepo outline: Packages, optional Related
Projects, and License. Installation and usage belong in package READMEs, which
use the CLI or library outline from `readme-md.yaml`.

Only `docgen-php`, `guard-php`, and `phpstan-guard-rules` maintain `docs/`.
The root, `phpstan-ai-formatter`, and `phpunit-ai-reporter` import `disable-doc`.
Agent skills live in their owning packages; do not recreate a root `skills/`.
Generated API sites go under `build/`.

- [DocGen](packages/docgen-php/docs/docgen.md): Commands, scope, caching, coverage, revision diffs, and local previews.
- [DocGen architecture](packages/docgen-php/docs/architecture.md): Generation pipeline and layer boundaries.
- [Guard policies](packages/guard-php/docs/policies.md): Checks, repairs, and adoption.
- [Guard command line](packages/guard-php/docs/cli.md): Commands, options, reports, and exit codes.
- [Guard configuration](packages/guard-php/docs/configuration.md): Imports, overrides, presets, and scope.
- [Guard metrics](packages/guard-php/docs/metrics.md): PHP line and complexity limits.
- [Guard structure](packages/guard-php/docs/structure.md): Directory contents, naming, and count constraints.
- [Guard documents](packages/guard-php/docs/documents.md): Markdown outlines, badges, and content rules.
- [Guard configuration fields](packages/guard-php/docs/fields.md): Field assertions and repairs.
- [Guard extensions](packages/guard-php/docs/extensions.md): Custom policies and structures.
- [PHPStan rules](packages/phpstan-guard-rules/docs/phpstan.md): Identifiers, configuration, Rector safety categories, and links to each rule.
- [Rector](packages/phpstan-guard-rules/docs/rector.md): Safe and risky automatic fixes.
- [PHPStan AI Formatter](packages/phpstan-ai-formatter/README.md): Setup and output modes.
- [PHPUnit AI Reporter and Doctest](packages/phpunit-ai-reporter/README.md): Setup, reporting, and executable examples.

# AGENTS

## Vision

Provide tools for AI-assisted PHP development that detect code, test, and configuration problems early and explain how to fix them. This repository is a monorepo of five Composer packages, each with its own dependencies and checks.

## Supported Versions

- **PHP**: 8.0 or later
- **PHPStan**: ^1.12 || ^2.0
- **PHPUnit**: ^9.6 || ^10.5 || ^11 || ^12 || ^13

## Architecture

| Package | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/guard-php` | Source, structure, documentation, and configuration policy checks and repairs. |
| `packages/docgen-php` | API documentation generation and site assets. |
| `packages/phpstan-guard-rules` | PHPStan rules and strict configuration. |
| `packages/phpunit-ai-reporter` | PHPUnit reporting, Doctest, and shared agent detection. |
| `packages/phpstan-ai-formatter` | PHPStan's `ai` error formatter. |

Run Composer commands in the owning package, for example
`composer --working-dir=packages/guard-php guard`. Each package provides `lint`,
`test`, and `test:unit` scripts. Check root documentation and structure with
`php packages/guard-php/bin/guard check --config=guard.yaml` after installing
Guard's dependencies.

### Branching Strategy

This project is developed on `main` only. Commit directly to `main`, whatever the size of the change.

- Do not create branches. A branch cannot be merged back here, so work left on one is stranded.
- Do not open pull requests. They are not part of this project's workflow.
- The common agent habit of branching before committing on a default branch does not apply here: `main` is the working branch.

### Rule Design Principles

- AI-friendly error messages: Every error message must clearly state *what is wrong* and *how to fix it*. An AI agent reading the message should be able to resolve the violation without additional context.
- Specific and identifiable: Messages must include enough detail (e.g., the offending symbol name, the expected pattern) so that each violation can be individually targeted in `ignoreErrors` configurations. Vague messages like "invalid code" are not acceptable.

## Documents

The root README follows Guard's monorepo outline: Packages, optional Related
Projects, and License. Installation and usage belong in package READMEs, which
use the CLI or library outline from `readme-md.yaml`.

Only `docgen-php`, `guard-php`, and `phpstan-guard-rules` maintain `docs/`.
The root, `phpstan-ai-formatter`, and `phpunit-ai-reporter` import `disable-doc`.
Agent skills live in their owning packages; do not recreate a root `skills/`.
Generated API sites go under `build/`.

- [DocGen](packages/docgen-php/docs/docgen.md): Commands, scope, caching, coverage, revision diffs, and local previews.
- [DocGen architecture](packages/docgen-php/docs/architecture.md): Generation pipeline and layer boundaries.
- [Guard policies](packages/guard-php/docs/policies.md): Checks, repairs, and adoption.
- [Guard command line](packages/guard-php/docs/cli.md): Commands, options, reports, and exit codes.
- [Guard configuration](packages/guard-php/docs/configuration.md): Imports, overrides, presets, and scope.
- [Guard metrics](packages/guard-php/docs/metrics.md): PHP line and complexity limits.
- [Guard structure](packages/guard-php/docs/structure.md): Directory contents, naming, and count constraints.
- [Guard documents](packages/guard-php/docs/documents.md): Markdown outlines, badges, and content rules.
- [Guard configuration fields](packages/guard-php/docs/fields.md): Field assertions and repairs.
- [Guard extensions](packages/guard-php/docs/extensions.md): Custom policies and structures.
- [PHPStan rules](packages/phpstan-guard-rules/docs/phpstan.md): Identifiers, configuration, Rector safety categories, and links to each rule.
- [Rector](packages/phpstan-guard-rules/docs/rector.md): Safe and risky automatic fixes.
- [PHPStan AI Formatter](packages/phpstan-ai-formatter/README.md): Setup and output modes.
- [PHPUnit AI Reporter and Doctest](packages/phpunit-ai-reporter/README.md): Setup, reporting, and executable examples.

# AGENTS

## Vision

Provide tools for AI-assisted PHP development that detect code, test, and configuration problems early and explain how to fix them. This repository is a monorepo of five Composer packages, each with its own dependencies and checks.

## Supported Versions

- **PHP**: 8.0 or later
- **PHPStan**: ^1.12 || ^2.0
- **PHPUnit**: ^9.6 || ^10.5 || ^11 || ^12 || ^13

## Architecture

| Package | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/guard-php` | Source, structure, documentation, and configuration policy checks and repairs. |
| `packages/docgen-php` | API documentation generation and site assets. |
| `packages/phpstan-guard-rules` | PHPStan rules and strict configuration. |
| `packages/phpunit-ai-reporter` | PHPUnit reporting, Doctest, and shared agent detection. |
| `packages/phpstan-ai-formatter` | PHPStan's `ai` error formatter. |

Run Composer commands in the owning package, for example
`composer --working-dir=packages/guard-php guard`. Each package provides `lint`,
`test`, and `test:unit` scripts. Check root documentation and structure with
`php packages/guard-php/bin/guard check --config=guard.yaml` after installing
Guard's dependencies.

### Branching Strategy

This project is developed on `main` only. Commit directly to `main`, whatever the size of the change.

- Do not create branches. A branch cannot be merged back here, so work left on one is stranded.
- Do not open pull requests. They are not part of this project's workflow.
- The common agent habit of branching before committing on a default branch does not apply here: `main` is the working branch.

### Rule Design Principles

- AI-friendly error messages: Every error message must clearly state *what is wrong* and *how to fix it*. An AI agent reading the message should be able to resolve the violation without additional context.
- Specific and identifiable: Messages must include enough detail (e.g., the offending symbol name, the expected pattern) so that each violation can be individually targeted in `ignoreErrors` configurations. Vague messages like "invalid code" are not acceptable.

## Documents

The root README follows Guard's monorepo outline: Packages, optional Related
Projects, and License. Installation and usage belong in package READMEs, which
use the CLI or library outline from `readme-md.yaml`.

Only `docgen-php`, `guard-php`, and `phpstan-guard-rules` maintain `docs/`.
The root, `phpstan-ai-formatter`, and `phpunit-ai-reporter` import `disable-doc`.
Agent skills live in their owning packages; do not recreate a root `skills/`.
Generated API sites go under `build/`.

- [DocGen](packages/docgen-php/docs/docgen.md): Commands, scope, caching, coverage, revision diffs, and local previews.
- [DocGen architecture](packages/docgen-php/docs/architecture.md): Generation pipeline and layer boundaries.
- [Guard policies](packages/guard-php/docs/policies.md): Checks, repairs, and adoption.
- [Guard command line](packages/guard-php/docs/cli.md): Commands, options, reports, and exit codes.
- [Guard configuration](packages/guard-php/docs/configuration.md): Imports, overrides, presets, and scope.
- [Guard metrics](packages/guard-php/docs/metrics.md): PHP line and complexity limits.
- [Guard structure](packages/guard-php/docs/structure.md): Directory contents, naming, and count constraints.
- [Guard documents](packages/guard-php/docs/documents.md): Markdown outlines, badges, and content rules.
- [Guard configuration fields](packages/guard-php/docs/fields.md): Field assertions and repairs.
- [Guard extensions](packages/guard-php/docs/extensions.md): Custom policies and structures.
- [PHPStan rules](packages/phpstan-guard-rules/docs/phpstan.md): Identifiers, configuration, Rector safety categories, and links to each rule.
- [Rector](packages/phpstan-guard-rules/docs/rector.md): Safe and risky automatic fixes.
- [PHPStan AI Formatter](packages/phpstan-ai-formatter/README.md): Setup and output modes.
- [PHPUnit AI Reporter and Doctest](packages/phpunit-ai-reporter/README.md): Setup, reporting, and executable examples.

# Rector Support

The package provides ten optional Rector rules: two safe transformations and
eight transformations that require review. Every PHPStan rule is classified in
the [rule list](phpstan.md); each rule page explains its supported cases,
risks, or reason automatic changes are unavailable.

Register the classes you want to run with `withRules()` in `rector.php`. Each
class can be enabled independently, including rules classified as risky.

## Installation

Install Rector in the consuming project:

```sh
composer require --dev rector/rector:^2.6.7
```

The supported Rector runtime is `^2.6.7` with PHP 8.0 or later. Rector 2 requires
PHPStan 2. The PHPStan extension itself still supports `^1.12 || ^2.0`, and
installing this package does not require Rector. Projects retaining PHPStan 1
must run Rector from a separate tool installation with this package installed.

## Safe Changes

Create `rector.php` in your project:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
    ]);
```

Preview the changes, then apply them:

```sh
vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run
vendor/bin/rector process
```

These two rules preserve executable behavior and documented contract contents in
the supported cases. They expand single-line public PHPDoc and add `#[Override]`
where the existing PHPStan rule confirms a valid concrete parent override.
The new attribute is observable through reflection; projects that instantiate
attributes on PHP before 8.3 need an `Override` polyfill or can select only the
PHPDoc rule. Line-number-sensitive code or tools may observe formatting changes.

## Risky Changes

Risky rules can change runtime behavior, declared types or exceptions, test
documentation, or analysis suppressions. Their implementation is deliberately
limited to specific patterns, and they leave unsupported cases unchanged.
Review the diff and run PHPStan and the test suite after applying them.

Add individual risky rule classes after reviewing their supported cases. This
example enables exception chaining alongside the two safe rules:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\RequireExceptionChainingRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
        RequireExceptionChainingRector::class,
    ]);
```

Only the selected classes run. PHPStan's `rules.neon` does not register Rector
rules automatically.

## Rule Classes

| PHPStan rule | Rector class in `Toolkit\Rector` | Category |
|-------------|----------------------------------|----------|
| [ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md#rector) | `ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector` | Safe |
| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md#rector) | `OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector` | Safe |
| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbidNonDocCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidEmptyCatchRule](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md#rector) | `ForbidEmptyCatchRector` | Risky |
| [RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule](rules/RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule.md#rector) | `RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRector` | Risky |
| [RequireExceptionChainingRule](rules/RequireExceptionChainingRule.md#rector) | `RequireExceptionChainingRector` | Risky |
| [RequireListForArrayLiteralRule](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md#rector) | `RequireListForArrayLiteralRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule](rules/ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule.md#rector) | `ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector` | Risky |

## Configuration

Rector does not read `parameters.toolkit` from `phpstan.neon`. Keep the selected
rules, paths, skips, and test namespace prefixes aligned with your PHPStan policy.
For custom restricted test namespaces, configure the prose-removal rule:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withConfiguredRule(ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector::class, [
        'Project\Tests\Unit',
        'Project\Tests\Integration',
    ]);
```

## Unavailable Changes

Rules classified as unavailable require decisions about domain types, public
APIs, dependency ownership, test scenarios, or meaningful assertions. The package
does not invent examples, remove assertions, widen visibility, or add arbitrary
dispatch branches to make those diagnostics disappear. Follow the manual repair
instructions on the corresponding rule page.

## Verification

The unit suite runs the real Rector CLI against before/after fixtures for every
provided transformation. It checks unchanged unsupported cases and runs Rector
again in dry-run mode to detect non-idempotent changes. Run it from the package:

```sh
composer test:unit -- --filter Rector
```

See the upstream [custom rule documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/custom-rule)
for class registration and Rector configuration concepts.
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Tests\Unit\Rector;

use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\CoversClass;
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\Large;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;
use Tests\Rector\RectorFixtureRunner;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;

/**
 * @covers \Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector
 * @large
 */
#[CoversClass(ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class)]
#[Large]
final class ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRectorTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testRefactorPreservesUnsupportedCasesAndIsIdempotent(): void
    {

final class RectorFixtureRunner

    /**
     * @return array{expected: string, actual: string, exitCode: int, output: string, idempotent: bool}
     */
    public function run(string $rule, string $fixture, string $set = ''): array
    {
        $root = dirname(__DIR__, 2);
        $contents = file_get_contents(__DIR__ . '/fixtures/' . $fixture . '.php.inc');
        if ($contents === false) {
            throw new RuntimeException('Cannot read Rector fixture ' . $fixture);
        }
        $parts = explode("\n-----\n", $contents, 2);
        $directory = sys_get_temp_dir() . '/toolkit-rector-' . bin2hex(random_bytes(8));
        mkdir($directory);
        $file = $directory . '/example.php';
        file_put_contents($file, $parts[0]);
        $command = [
            PHP_BINARY, $root . '/vendor/bin/rector', 'process', $file,
            '--config', __DIR__ . '/config.php', '--no-progress-bar', '--no-diffs', '--clear-cache',
        ];
        $environment = [
            'TOOLKIT_RECTOR_RULE' => $rule,
            'TOOLKIT_RECTOR_SET' => $set,
            'TOOLKIT_RECTOR_CACHE' => $directory . '/cache',
            'XDEBUG_MODE' => 'off',
        ];
        $process = new Process($command, $root, $environment);
        $process->setTimeout(60);
        try {
            $exitCode = $process->run();
            $output = $process->getOutput() . $process->getErrorOutput();
            $actual = file_get_contents($file);
            $again = new Process([...$command, '--dry-run'], $root, $environment);
            $again->setTimeout(60);
            $idempotent = $again->run() === 0;

            return [
                'expected' => $parts[1] ?? $parts[0],
                'actual' => $actual === false ? '' : $actual,
                'exitCode' => $exitCode,
                'output' => $output . $again->getOutput() . $again->getErrorOutput(),
                'idempotent' => $idempotent,
            ];
        } finally {
            (new Filesystem())->remove($directory);
        }
    }

# AGENTS

## Vision

Provide tools for AI-assisted PHP development that detect code, test, and configuration problems early and explain how to fix them. This repository is a monorepo of five Composer packages, each with its own dependencies and checks.

## Supported Versions

- **PHP**: 8.0 or later
- **PHPStan**: ^1.12 || ^2.0
- **PHPUnit**: ^9.6 || ^10.5 || ^11 || ^12 || ^13

## Architecture

| Package | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/guard-php` | Source, structure, documentation, and configuration policy checks and repairs. |
| `packages/docgen-php` | API documentation generation and site assets. |
| `packages/phpstan-guard-rules` | PHPStan rules and strict configuration. |
| `packages/phpunit-ai-reporter` | PHPUnit reporting, Doctest, and shared agent detection. |
| `packages/phpstan-ai-formatter` | PHPStan's `ai` error formatter. |

Run Composer commands in the owning package, for example
`composer --working-dir=packages/guard-php guard`. Each package provides `lint`,
`test`, and `test:unit` scripts. Check root documentation and structure with
`php packages/guard-php/bin/guard check --config=guard.yaml` after installing
Guard's dependencies.

### Branching Strategy

This project is developed on `main` only. Commit directly to `main`, whatever the size of the change.

- Do not create branches. A branch cannot be merged back here, so work left on one is stranded.
- Do not open pull requests. They are not part of this project's workflow.
- The common agent habit of branching before committing on a default branch does not apply here: `main` is the working branch.

### Rule Design Principles

- AI-friendly error messages: Every error message must clearly state *what is wrong* and *how to fix it*. An AI agent reading the message should be able to resolve the violation without additional context.
- Specific and identifiable: Messages must include enough detail (e.g., the offending symbol name, the expected pattern) so that each violation can be individually targeted in `ignoreErrors` configurations. Vague messages like "invalid code" are not acceptable.

## Documents

The root README follows Guard's monorepo outline: Packages, optional Related
Projects, and License. Installation and usage belong in package READMEs, which
use the CLI or library outline from `readme-md.yaml`.

Only `docgen-php`, `guard-php`, and `phpstan-guard-rules` maintain `docs/`.
The root, `phpstan-ai-formatter`, and `phpunit-ai-reporter` import `disable-doc`.
Agent skills live in their owning packages; do not recreate a root `skills/`.
Generated API sites go under `build/`.

- [DocGen](packages/docgen-php/docs/docgen.md): Commands, scope, caching, coverage, revision diffs, and local previews.
- [DocGen architecture](packages/docgen-php/docs/architecture.md): Generation pipeline and layer boundaries.
- [Guard policies](packages/guard-php/docs/policies.md): Checks, repairs, and adoption.
- [Guard command line](packages/guard-php/docs/cli.md): Commands, options, reports, and exit codes.
- [Guard configuration](packages/guard-php/docs/configuration.md): Imports, overrides, presets, and scope.
- [Guard metrics](packages/guard-php/docs/metrics.md): PHP line and complexity limits.
- [Guard structure](packages/guard-php/docs/structure.md): Directory contents, naming, and count constraints.
- [Guard documents](packages/guard-php/docs/documents.md): Markdown outlines, badges, and content rules.
- [Guard configuration fields](packages/guard-php/docs/fields.md): Field assertions and repairs.
- [Guard extensions](packages/guard-php/docs/extensions.md): Custom policies and structures.
- [PHPStan rules](packages/phpstan-guard-rules/docs/phpstan.md): Identifiers, configuration, Rector safety categories, and links to each rule.
- [Rector](packages/phpstan-guard-rules/docs/rector.md): Safe and risky automatic fixes.
- [PHPStan AI Formatter](packages/phpstan-ai-formatter/README.md): Setup and output modes.
- [PHPUnit AI Reporter and Doctest](packages/phpunit-ai-reporter/README.md): Setup, reporting, and executable examples.

# Rector Support

The package provides ten optional Rector rules: two safe transformations and
eight transformations that require review. Every PHPStan rule is classified in
the [rule list](phpstan.md); each rule page explains its supported cases,
risks, or reason automatic changes are unavailable.

Register the classes you want to run with `withRules()` in `rector.php`. Each
class can be enabled independently, including rules classified as risky.

## Installation

Install Rector in the consuming project:

```sh
composer require --dev rector/rector:^2.6.7
```

The supported Rector runtime is `^2.6.7` with PHP 8.0 or later. Rector 2 requires
PHPStan 2. The PHPStan extension itself still supports `^1.12 || ^2.0`, and
installing this package does not require Rector. Projects retaining PHPStan 1
must run Rector from a separate tool installation with this package installed.

## Safe Changes

Create `rector.php` in your project:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
    ]);
```

Preview the changes, then apply them:

```sh
vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run
vendor/bin/rector process
```

These two rules preserve executable behavior and documented contract contents in
the supported cases. They expand single-line public PHPDoc and add `#[Override]`
where the existing PHPStan rule confirms a valid concrete parent override.
The new attribute is observable through reflection; projects that instantiate
attributes on PHP before 8.3 need an `Override` polyfill or can select only the
PHPDoc rule. Line-number-sensitive code or tools may observe formatting changes.

## Risky Changes

Risky rules can change runtime behavior, declared types or exceptions, test
documentation, or analysis suppressions. Their implementation is deliberately
limited to specific patterns, and they leave unsupported cases unchanged.
Review the diff and run PHPStan and the test suite after applying them.

Add individual risky rule classes after reviewing their supported cases. This
example enables exception chaining alongside the two safe rules:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\RequireExceptionChainingRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
        RequireExceptionChainingRector::class,
    ]);
```

Only the selected classes run. PHPStan's `rules.neon` does not register Rector
rules automatically.

## Rule Classes

| PHPStan rule | Rector class in `Toolkit\Rector` | Category |
|-------------|----------------------------------|----------|
| [ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md#rector) | `ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector` | Safe |
| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md#rector) | `OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector` | Safe |
| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbidNonDocCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidEmptyCatchRule](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md#rector) | `ForbidEmptyCatchRector` | Risky |
| [RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule](rules/RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule.md#rector) | `RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRector` | Risky |
| [RequireExceptionChainingRule](rules/RequireExceptionChainingRule.md#rector) | `RequireExceptionChainingRector` | Risky |
| [RequireListForArrayLiteralRule](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md#rector) | `RequireListForArrayLiteralRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule](rules/ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule.md#rector) | `ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector` | Risky |

## Configuration

Rector does not read `parameters.toolkit` from `phpstan.neon`. Keep the selected
rules, paths, skips, and test namespace prefixes aligned with your PHPStan policy.
For custom restricted test namespaces, configure the prose-removal rule:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withConfiguredRule(ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector::class, [
        'Project\Tests\Unit',
        'Project\Tests\Integration',
    ]);
```

## Unavailable Changes

Rules classified as unavailable require decisions about domain types, public
APIs, dependency ownership, test scenarios, or meaningful assertions. The package
does not invent examples, remove assertions, widen visibility, or add arbitrary
dispatch branches to make those diagnostics disappear. Follow the manual repair
instructions on the corresponding rule page.

## Verification

The unit suite runs the real Rector CLI against before/after fixtures for every
provided transformation. It checks unchanged unsupported cases and runs Rector
again in dry-run mode to detect non-idempotent changes. Run it from the package:

```sh
composer test:unit -- --filter Rector
```

See the upstream [custom rule documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/custom-rule)
for class registration and Rector configuration concepts.

        self::assertSame(0, $result['exitCode'], $result['output']);
        self::assertSame($result['expected'], $result['actual']);
        self::assertTrue($result['idempotent'], 'A second Rector run must have no diff.');

All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

# phpstan-guard-rules

[![PHP](https://img.shields.io/badge/php-8.0%2B-777bb4?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://www.php.net/)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](../../LICENSE)

Strict PHPStan rules for AI-assisted PHP development, covering production code,
public API contracts, and test design.
Part of [php-ai-toolkit](../../README.md).

## Requirements

- PHP 8.0 or later.
- PHPStan `^1.12 || ^2.0`.
- Composer.

## Installation

From a local checkout, register the packages in the consuming project:

```sh
composer config repositories.php-ai-toolkit path '../php-ai-toolkit/packages/*'
composer config minimum-stability dev
composer config prefer-stable true
composer require --dev k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules:dev-main
```

Adjust the checkout path for your project.

## Usage

Include the shipped rules and PHPStan's strict rules in `phpstan.neon`:

```neon
includes:
    - vendor/phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules/rules.neon
    - vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rules.neon

parameters:
    level: max
    paths:
        - src
        - tests
```

Adjust the analysis paths to your project, then run `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`.
If `phpstan/extension-installer` already loads these files, avoid including them twice.

Optional [Rector support](docs/rector.md) provides safe and risky rule classes.
Install `rector/rector:^2.6.7` and select the rules in `rector.php`:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
    ]);
```

Preview changes with `vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run`. Add risky rule classes
only after reviewing their behavioral or contract changes. The rule reference
records automatic-fix availability for every rule.

## Documentation

The [rule reference](docs/phpstan.md) lists identifiers, configuration,
Rector safety categories, and links to each rule. The [PHPStan setup skill](skills/setup-toolkit-phpstan/SKILL.md)
also configures the separate AI formatter.

## License

[MIT](../../LICENSE)
# Rector Support

The package provides ten optional Rector rules: two safe transformations and
eight transformations that require review. Every PHPStan rule is classified in
the [rule list](phpstan.md); each rule page explains its supported cases,
risks, or reason automatic changes are unavailable.

Register the classes you want to run with `withRules()` in `rector.php`. Each
class can be enabled independently, including rules classified as risky.

## Installation

Install Rector in the consuming project:

```sh
composer require --dev rector/rector:^2.6.7
```

The supported Rector runtime is `^2.6.7` with PHP 8.0 or later. Rector 2 requires
PHPStan 2. The PHPStan extension itself still supports `^1.12 || ^2.0`, and
installing this package does not require Rector. Projects retaining PHPStan 1
must run Rector from a separate tool installation with this package installed.

## Safe Changes

Create `rector.php` in your project:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
    ]);
```

Preview the changes, then apply them:

```sh
vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run
vendor/bin/rector process
```

These two rules preserve executable behavior and documented contract contents in
the supported cases. They expand single-line public PHPDoc and add `#[Override]`
where the existing PHPStan rule confirms a valid concrete parent override.
The new attribute is observable through reflection; projects that instantiate
attributes on PHP before 8.3 need an `Override` polyfill or can select only the
PHPDoc rule. Line-number-sensitive code or tools may observe formatting changes.

## Risky Changes

Risky rules can change runtime behavior, declared types or exceptions, test
documentation, or analysis suppressions. Their implementation is deliberately
limited to specific patterns, and they leave unsupported cases unchanged.
Review the diff and run PHPStan and the test suite after applying them.

Add individual risky rule classes after reviewing their supported cases. This
example enables exception chaining alongside the two safe rules:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\RequireExceptionChainingRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
        RequireExceptionChainingRector::class,
    ]);
```

Only the selected classes run. PHPStan's `rules.neon` does not register Rector
rules automatically.

## Rule Classes

| PHPStan rule | Rector class in `Toolkit\Rector` | Category |
|-------------|----------------------------------|----------|
| [ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md#rector) | `ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector` | Safe |
| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md#rector) | `OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector` | Safe |
| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbidNonDocCommentRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidEmptyCatchRule](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md#rector) | `ForbidEmptyCatchRector` | Risky |
| [RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule](rules/RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule.md#rector) | `RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRector` | Risky |
| [RequireExceptionChainingRule](rules/RequireExceptionChainingRule.md#rector) | `RequireExceptionChainingRector` | Risky |
| [RequireListForArrayLiteralRule](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md#rector) | `RequireListForArrayLiteralRector` | Risky |
| [ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule](rules/ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule.md#rector) | `ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector` | Risky |

## Configuration

Rector does not read `parameters.toolkit` from `phpstan.neon`. Keep the selected
rules, paths, skips, and test namespace prefixes aligned with your PHPStan policy.
For custom restricted test namespaces, configure the prose-removal rule:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withConfiguredRule(ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector::class, [
        'Project\Tests\Unit',
        'Project\Tests\Integration',
    ]);
```

## Unavailable Changes

Rules classified as unavailable require decisions about domain types, public
APIs, dependency ownership, test scenarios, or meaningful assertions. The package
does not invent examples, remove assertions, widen visibility, or add arbitrary
dispatch branches to make those diagnostics disappear. Follow the manual repair
instructions on the corresponding rule page.

## Verification

The unit suite runs the real Rector CLI against before/after fixtures for every
provided transformation. It checks unchanged unsupported cases and runs Rector
again in dry-run mode to detect non-idempotent changes. Run it from the package:

```sh
composer test:unit -- --filter Rector
```

See the upstream [custom rule documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/custom-rule)
for class registration and Rector configuration concepts.
# PHPStan Rules

Custom PHPStan rules provided by php-ai-toolkit. Each rule detects anti-patterns that actually occur in AI-generated code.

## Rector Support

Every rule below is classified as **Safe**, **Risky**, or **Unavailable** for automatic
changes. Enable the transformations you need by registering their Rector classes
with `withRules()` in `rector.php`.
A classification describes only the supported cases; each rule’s Rector section
lists skipped cases and review requirements. See [Rector setup](rector.md).

The legacy opt-in [ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule](rules/ForbidMixedArrayReturnTypeRule.md#rector)
is also classified as **Unavailable**. Internal helper rules for mixed types and
class dispatch share their parent rule’s classification.

## General

Rules applied to all code.

| Rule | Description | Error Identifier | Rector |
|------|-------------|------------------|--------|
| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md) | Forbids `@phpstan-ignore` and `@infection-ignore-all` comments | `customRules.phpstanIgnoreComment`, `customRules.infectionIgnoreAllComment` | [Risky](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) |
| [ForbidFileTermRule](rules/ForbidFileTermRule.md) | Forbids configured literal terms in files matching restricted path patterns | `customRules.forbiddenFileTerm` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidFileTermRule.md#rector) |
| [ForbidDependencyRule](rules/ForbidDependencyRule.md) | Forbids symbol and file-reading dependencies between configured paths; allows each root directory to depend only on itself and src by default | `customRules.forbiddenDependency` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidDependencyRule.md#rector) |
| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md) | Forbids direct calls to magic methods | `customRules.forbiddenMagicMethodCall` | [Risky](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md#rector) |
| [ForbiddenNamespaceRule](rules/ForbiddenNamespaceRule.md) | Forbids configured namespace prefixes such as `Tests\Support`, `Tests\Helper`, `Tests\Util`, and `Tests\Fixture` | `customRules.forbiddenNamespace` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbiddenNamespaceRule.md#rector) |
| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md) | Requires `#[Override]` attribute on overridden methods | `customRules.overrideMustHaveAttribute` | [Safe](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md#rector) |
| [SrcUnitTestPairRule](rules/SrcUnitTestPairRule.md) | Enforces 1:1 pairing between `src/` classes and `tests/Unit/` test classes | `customRules.srcUnitTestPair` | [Unavailable](rules/SrcUnitTestPairRule.md#rector) |
| [RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule](rules/RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule.md) | Requires PHPDoc on all public API elements | `customRules.requirePhpDocOnPublicApi` | [Unavailable](rules/RequirePhpDocOnPublicApiRule.md#rector) |
| [RequireExampleOnPublicApiRule](rules/RequireExampleOnPublicApiRule.md) | Requires a runnable `@example` on declarations marked `@visibility public` | `customRules.requireExampleOnClass`, `customRules.requireExampleOnMethod`, `customRules.requireExampleOnProperty`, `customRules.requireExampleOnConstant`, `customRules.requireExampleOnEnumCase` | [Unavailable](rules/RequireExampleOnPublicApiRule.md#rector) |
| [EnforceVisibilityScopeRule](rules/EnforceVisibilityScopeRule.md) | Enforces namespace visibility scopes declared with `@visibility` and treats explicitly public API as externally used | `customRules.visibilityInvalidScope`, `customRules.visibilityOutOfScope` | [Unavailable](rules/EnforceVisibilityScopeRule.md#rector) |

| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md) | Forbids `/* */` and `#` comments everywhere, and `//` comments outside `catch` blocks and array literals; `/** */` PHPDoc is allowed | `customRules.forbidNonDocComment` | [Risky](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md#rector) |
| [ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md) | Forbids single-line PHPDoc on public elements; requires multi-line format | `customRules.forbidSingleLinePhpDoc` | [Safe](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md#rector) |
| [ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule](rules/ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule.md) | Forbids configured suffixes on class, interface, trait, and enum names | `customRules.forbiddenClassLikeNameSuffix` | [Unavailable](rules/ForbidClassLikeNameSuffixRule.md#rector) |
| [NoNonPublicMethodRule](rules/NoNonPublicMethodRule.md) | Forbids private methods and forbids protected methods outside abstract classes, traits, and override methods; constructors are exempt | `customRules.nonPublicMethod` | [Unavailable](rules/NoNonPublicMethodRule.md#rector) |

Rules inherit `toolkit.allRules`, which defaults to `true`, except mutation
contracts, which are opt-in so an existing unannotated project does not change
semantics on upgrade. Override a specific rule through its `enabled` value:

```neon
parameters:
    toolkit:
        forbidEmptyCatch:
            enabled: false
```

Set `allRules: false` to make every rule opt-in. Toolkit adoption keeps the
default; changing a switch is an explicit project policy decision.

Enable mutation contracts explicitly with `toolkit.mutation.enabled: true`.

## Redundant PHPStan Diagnostics

The toolkit suppresses a PHPStan or Strict Rules diagnostic only when an enabled
toolkit rule makes that diagnostic non-actionable. The toolkit error remains as
the single instruction for fixing the prohibited construct:

| Enabled toolkit rule | Suppressed diagnostic | Scope |
|----------------------|-----------------------|-------|
| `noNonPublicMethod` | `method.unused`, `method.finalPrivate` | Private method declarations; PHPStan does not emit either for constructors, and `consistentConstructor.private` stays visible because the rule exempts constructors |
| `noPrivateMethodInTestClass` | The same private-method diagnostics | Restricted test classes |
| `noPropertyInTestClass` | `property.unused`, `property.neverRead`, `property.neverWritten`, `property.onlyRead`, `property.onlyWritten` | Restricted test classes |
| `noClassConstantInTestClass` | `classConstant.unused` | Restricted test classes |
| `noControlFlowInTestMethod` | PHPStan and Strict Rules diagnostics emitted for the prohibited `if`, loop, `switch`, or `match` node | Test methods in restricted test classes |
| `requireThrowsTagOnDirectThrow` | `missingType.checkedException` | Direct escaping throws in methods; propagated checked exceptions remain reported |

This is semantic suppression through PHPStan's extension API, not a global
`ignoreErrors` entry. Disabling the dominating toolkit rule automatically

[![PHP](https://img.shields.io/badge/php-8.0%2B-777bb4?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://www.php.net/)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](../../LICENSE)

Strict PHPStan rules for AI-assisted PHP development, covering production code,
public API contracts, and test design.
Part of [php-ai-toolkit](../../README.md).

## Requirements

- PHP 8.0 or later.
- PHPStan `^1.12 || ^2.0`.
- Composer.

## Installation

From a local checkout, register the packages in the consuming project:

```sh
composer config repositories.php-ai-toolkit path '../php-ai-toolkit/packages/*'
composer config minimum-stability dev
composer config prefer-stable true
composer require --dev k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules:dev-main
```

Adjust the checkout path for your project.

## Usage

Include the shipped rules and PHPStan's strict rules in `phpstan.neon`:

```neon
includes:
    - vendor/phpstan/phpstan-strict-rules/rules.neon
    - vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rules.neon

parameters:
    level: max
    paths:
        - src
        - tests
```

Adjust the analysis paths to your project, then run `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse`.
If `phpstan/extension-installer` already loads these files, avoid including them twice.

Optional [Rector support](docs/rector.md) provides safe and risky rule classes.
Install `rector/rector:^2.6.7` and select the rules in `rector.php`:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
    ]);
```

Preview changes with `vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run`. Add risky rule classes
only after reviewing their behavioral or contract changes. The rule reference
records automatic-fix availability for every rule.

## Documentation

The [rule reference](docs/phpstan.md) lists identifiers, configuration,
Rector safety categories, and links to each rule. The [PHPStan setup skill](skills/setup-toolkit-phpstan/SKILL.md)
also configures the separate AI formatter.

# Rector Support

The package provides ten optional Rector rules: two safe transformations and
eight transformations that require review. Every PHPStan rule is classified in
the [rule list](phpstan.md); each rule page explains its supported cases,
risks, or reason automatic changes are unavailable.

Register the classes you want to run with `withRules()` in `rector.php`. Each
class can be enabled independently, including rules classified as risky.

## Installation

Install Rector in the consuming project:

```sh
composer require --dev rector/rector:^2.6.7
```

The supported Rector runtime is `^2.6.7` with PHP 8.0 or later. Rector 2 requires
PHPStan 2. The PHPStan extension itself still supports `^1.12 || ^2.0`, and
installing this package does not require Rector. Projects retaining PHPStan 1
must run Rector from a separate tool installation with this package installed.

## Safe Changes

Create `rector.php` in your project:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
    ]);
```

Preview the changes, then apply them:

```sh
vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run
vendor/bin/rector process
```

These two rules preserve executable behavior and documented contract contents in
the supported cases. They expand single-line public PHPDoc and add `#[Override]`
where the existing PHPStan rule confirms a valid concrete parent override.
The new attribute is observable through reflection; projects that instantiate
attributes on PHP before 8.3 need an `Override` polyfill or can select only the
PHPDoc rule. Line-number-sensitive code or tools may observe formatting changes.

## Risky Changes

Risky rules can change runtime behavior, declared types or exceptions, test
documentation, or analysis suppressions. Their implementation is deliberately
limited to specific patterns, and they leave unsupported cases unchanged.
Review the diff and run PHPStan and the test suite after applying them.

Add individual risky rule classes after reviewing their supported cases. This
example enables exception chaining alongside the two safe rules:

```php
<?php

use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector;
use Toolkit\Rector\RequireExceptionChainingRector;

return RectorConfig::configure()
    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
    ->withRules([
        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
        OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector::class,
        RequireExceptionChainingRector::class,
    ]);
```

Only the selected classes run. PHPStan's `rules.neon` does not register Rector
rules automatically.
